An open order closed. closed_reason says why: paid, closed_by_merchant, checkout_expired, written_off, superseded, or return_resolution_canceled.
An order has an inventory failure that requires operator action.
An order inventory exception was resolved.
An order became fully paid, including by a manual payment on its invoice. Use payment_intent.succeeded for each successful online payment.
An order first became partially paid, including by a manual payment on its invoice. Use payment_intent.succeeded for each successful online payment.
A shipment package changed, including status, details, or contents. List the package items to read its contents.
A partner app install was created.
An environment grant's permissions changed: the merchant re-authorized, or you removed or narrowed a permission.
The install was revoked by the merchant or by you. revoked_by says which.
A payment intent authorization expired before capture.
A payment intent fulfillment hold was activated or released.
A payment was submitted and is awaiting its final outcome.
The payment requires a customer action such as 3D Secure authentication.
The payment was authorized and is awaiting capture.
A payment intent changed without entering a more specific lifecycle status.
A payment link changed, including being activated or deactivated. Sales through the link don't send this event.
A payment method became active and can be charged.
A saved payment method was deleted. It stays readable and can't be charged again.
A payment review was resolved or closed by a payment lifecycle change.
A payment was placed into manual review.
A declined review's refund failed, so the review is open again and needs a decision.
A payout to the merchant's bank was canceled.
A payout to the merchant's bank was created.
A payout failed and funds were returned to the balance.
A payout arrived at the merchant's bank.
A payout destination was removed. It stays readable by ID with status archived.
A payout destination (bank account) was added.
The merchant's payout schedule or settings changed.
A product was archived. Its variants were archived with it and send no events of their own.
A product was created. Each variant it created sends product_variant.created.

A product's own fields, options, images, categories or modifier set changed. Variant changes send product_variant events instead, although they also change the product's rollups and version. Rollups (default_variant, price_range, active_variant_count, variant_count, available_for_sale and delivery_configuration_status) and copied category names and handles send no product events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A variant was archived on its own. Archiving its product sends only product.archived.

A product variant was updated. Copied selected option names and values, available_for_sale, effective_images and delivery readiness send no variant events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A promotion was archived. Its codes were archived with it and send no events of their own.
A promotion was created. Each code it created sends promotion_code.created.

A promotion was updated. Changes to codes_summary, uses_count, available and unavailable_reason, including redemptions and schedule boundaries, send no promotion events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A promotion code was archived on its own. Archiving its promotion sends only promotion.archived.

A promotion code was updated. Changes to uses_count, available and unavailable_reason, including redemptions and schedule boundaries, send no promotion code events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A refund changed without entering a more specific lifecycle status.
An asynchronous report reached a terminal generation failure.
An asynchronous report completed and its authenticated CSV download is ready.
A Return completed after every required merchandise and buyer-value obligation cleared.
The merchant or policy automation recorded line-level Return decisions.
A completed Return was reopened for additional work.
A Return or one of its line-level progress projections changed.
A merchandise disposition was recorded for a Return.
A Return disposition changed execution state.
Acceptance was decided for a Return inspection observation.
A Return inspection observation was recorded.
A Return inspection observation was superseded by an auditable correction.
A Return receipt observation was recorded.
A Return receipt observation was superseded by an auditable correction.
An unmatched Return receipt line was verified against the expected merchandise.
A proposed buyer-value resolution was created for a Return.
A Return resolution changed proposal, gate, effect, or fulfillment state.
A shipment changed, including status, details, or package count.
A subscription's first paid period was collected, or it was created already paid or imported, so it is active. Sent once per subscription.
A subscription was set to cancel at the end of its billing period.
A subscription billing cycle was skipped without a charge.
A subscription renewal needs an address, method, or rate correction before it can be charged.
A subscription delivery hold is approaching its pause date.
A subscription's delivery preference changed. Paid, unshipped renewals keep their existing destination.
A subscription used its automatic payment retry budget.
A subscription renewal failed and is past due.
A subscription moved to another plan, or to its plan's current lines and prices. When the change bills a new period, subscription.payment_succeeded is sent with it.
A subscription's scheduled cancellation was undone, so it renews as usual.
A subscription trial is approaching its end.
A subscription changed and no more specific subscription event describes the change.
A subscription delivery method migration finished. Its counts and failures identify which subscriptions moved.
A subscription payment retry was created.

payload_version.description: 2 for every current event. 1 only for an event queued before 2026-10-16 and delivered afterwards, which keeps its previous data shape.

test.description: true for a synthetic event sent from the test-events endpoint, false otherwise.

PauseSubscriptionRequest.description: The request body for: Pause one of the current buyer's subscriptions; Pause subscription.

pause_duration_cycles.description: Billing cycles to pause for, at least 1. Omit it to pause until the subscription is resumed. A pause with a duration resumes automatically at scheduled_resume_at. Repeating the same pause length returns the paused subscription; changing the length requires resuming first. When the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities.pause.max_cycles is set, a buyer must send a value from 1 to that limit.

PayOrderRequest.description: The request body for: Pay order.

buyer_contact.description: Buyer email and phone recorded on the order. A checkout session payment uses the session's saved contact for omitted fields. Email and phone cannot be null.

expected_outstanding_money.description: The outstanding balance you reviewed. Required with checkout credentials, and with an API key or partner token when the order has an open checkout session. Optional otherwise.

expected_version.description: Optional version from the order you reviewed. A mismatch returns ORDER_CHANGED_REFRESH_REQUIRED, even when the outstanding amount is unchanged. Starting a payment advances the order's version. After a declined or failed attempt, use the order returned in the pay response or read the order again before retrying. When accepted_gift_card_allocation is sent, its order_version must match this value.

save_payment_method.description: The buyer's choice to save the card they typed for faster checkout at this merchant. Send true only from the checkout session's own credential, when the session's can_save_payment_method is true and save_payment_method_requires_verification is false, for one newly collected card sent as stripe.confirmation_token created with setup_future_usage on_session. The card is saved with usage on_session once the payment succeeds, for the customer the checkout acts for: the customer the merchant created the session for, or the customer whose email the buyer confirmed in it. A typed buyer_contact.email never decides it. A checkout that acts for no customer refuses the save until the buyer confirms their email with a code, unless it sends save_payment_method_phone. A checkout the buyer bound by a texted code saves the card with that number. A checkout whose buyer confirmed the customer's email can also send save_payment_method_phone, to save the card with a number the buyer confirms by text after paying. A checkout can send the buyer's choice with every payment button: Apple Pay, Google Pay, a bank account, or Affirm, in stripe.confirmation_token created with no setup_future_usage, pays without the save, and the payment attempt's payment_method_save reports not_saved with reason payment_method_not_saveable. The session's save_payment_method_types lists what is saved. Send false or omit it when the buyer does not choose to save; stripe.confirmation_token must then have no setup_future_usage.

save_payment_method_phone.description: A US or Canadian mobile phone number in E.164 format, such as +14155552671, that confirms a card saved while the checkout acts for no customer, or for the customer whose email the buyer confirmed in it. Send it with save_payment_method: true only from the checkout session's own credential, when the session's can_save_payment_method_with_phone is true. The card is kept for the customer the checkout acts for, or else the merchant's customer with the buyer's email, once the payment succeeds, or once it is approved when the merchant captures later, but works for nothing until the buyer confirms it within 24 hours, with a code texted to this number or, when the customer's email is the email of the payment, emailed there instead: request the code with POST /v1/checkout-sessions/{checkout_session_id}/customer-verifications and purpose confirm_saved_payment_method, and read payment_method_save on the checkout session. A card saved with the number makes it the customer's saved number, and the cards saved with the number it replaces are removed. A card not confirmed in time is not saved.

PayOrderResult.description: The order is the primary resource and expected_version target; order_payment_attempt records the payment outcome.

PaymentAddOnFee.description: A Flint fee added to a payment intent, with the fee type and amount.

PaymentAttemptGiftCardRedemption.description: A gift card redemption made as part of an order payment attempt, with the amount, tip, and gift card.

last4.description: Last four characters of the card's current code.

PaymentAttemptPaymentIntent.description: A payment intent used as one leg of an order payment attempt, with its amount, status, tip, and latest error.

amount_money.description: The amount requested from the buyer, including any tip_money. Capturing doesn't change it: after a partial capture it still shows the requested amount, and captured_money shows what was collected. On a standalone payment intent, PATCH can change it only before the first confirmation attempt.

authorization_expires_at.description: Capture is unavailable at or after this time, even if the payment still has requires_capture status.

capturable_money.description: Payment intent's stored capturable amount. A positive amount does not override authorization_expires_at or the payment status.

payment_intent_id.description: Flint payment intent ID.

selected_payment_option.description: Payment option used by this leg, using the same values as PaymentIntent.selected_payment_option. Fixed when the attempt becomes terminal. Omitted when no payment option has been selected.

status.description: Lifecycle status. requires_payment_method covers both a new payment intent and one whose last attempt failed, so read last_payment_error with it. succeeded, canceled, and expired are final. Refunds and disputes never change status.
x-enum-descriptions: Waiting for the buyer's payment details. Either nothing has been attempted yet, or the last attempt was declined, failed, or blocked and last_payment_error says why. Confirm again with a new credential.

Payment details are attached, but confirmation hasn't finished. Flint usually confirms in the same request that attaches them, so this status is brief unless that confirmation was interrupted. Resume the order's payment attempt, or call confirm with an empty body for a standalone payment intent. The payment_intent.updated event reports changes into this status.

The buyer must finish a step, such as 3D Secure authentication or a redirect, before the payment can continue. The confirm result's current_payment_action describes a standalone payment's step; call confirm with an empty body to retrieve it again. Afterward, call confirm with an empty body, or resume the order's payment attempt.

Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly. A processing payment intent can't be canceled or updated.
A manual-capture hold is in place and no money has been collected. Capture up to capturable_money, or cancel, before authorization_expires_at.
Canceled before any money was collected, by you or by Flint, for example when an invoice is voided. Final. cancellation_reason says why when Flint knows it. A canceled hold is in released_money.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final.
A manual-capture hold reached authorization_expires_at without a capture, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. The payment_intent.expired event reports it; cancellation_reason is absent.

PaymentClientAction.description: Typed provider-specific browser action payload. Execute the selected provider action before continuing the owning payment through Flint.

PaymentCollection.description: Client-side details for collecting payment from the buyer, such as the Stripe settings to initialize Stripe.js.

stripe.description: Client configuration for collecting the payment through Stripe.

PaymentCollectionStripe.description: Stripe details for collecting payment in the browser: account ID, publishable key, return URL, and Elements options.

account_id.description: Stripe account to use when initializing the payment client.

elements.description: Stripe Elements configuration for the available payment methods and amounts.

publishable_key.description: Publishable Stripe key for initializing the payment client.

return_url.description: URL the buyer returns to after a redirect payment step.

PaymentCollectionStripeElements.description: Stripe Elements collection guidance. Follow next_step in the browser, then submit the result to submit_to through Flint.

amount_money.description: Amount and currency used to initialize the payment form.

digital_wallets.description: Digital wallets that the payment form can offer.

mode.description: Whether Elements is collecting a payment source for an immediate payment or a setup source for future use.

next_step.description: Browser collection operation to perform before calling submit_to.

payment_method_creation.description: Stripe Elements payment method creation mode. Follow next_step: standalone PaymentIntents and checkout-authenticated order collection create a ConfirmationToken, while merchant-authenticated order collection and setup collection create a PaymentMethod.

payment_method_options.description: Payment method settings passed to the payment form.

payment_method_types.description: Payment method types that the payment form can offer.

selectable_payment_intents.description: Order payment intents that the buyer can select for collection.

submit_to.description: Flint operation that accepts the result of next_step.

PaymentErrorSummary.description: A summary of why a payment attempt failed, with a normalized error code, a message, the failure time, and remediation.

code.description: Flint-normalized payment failure code. Unknown provider values are returned as payment_failed.

failed_at.description: Time the payment attempt concluded in failure.

message.description: Flint-authored merchant-facing payment failure message. This is stable explanatory text, not raw provider copy.

remediation.description: Guidance for resolving the payment failure before trying to collect again.

PaymentFulfillmentHold.description: A hold on fulfillment tied to a payment, with the reason, the action required, and whether the hold is active or released.

PaymentIntent.description: One payment from a buyer, standalone or as a leg of an order. amount_money is the amount requested. Once the payment is authorized, authorized_money equals amount_money and splits into captured_money (collected), capturable_money (still on hold), and released_money (returned without being charged), so authorized_money always equals the sum of those three. Reconcile revenue from captured_money.

add_on_fees.description: Itemized invoice, subscription, and automatic tax fees collected with this payment. Available to the merchant only. Empty until fees settle or when no add-ons apply. Refunds do not return or revise these fees. Absent until Flint has determined and verified the fee. If Flint can't verify it when you read the payment intent, the field is omitted rather than shown unverified; read the payment intent again later.

amount_money.description: The amount requested from the buyer, including any tip_money. Capturing doesn't change it: after a partial capture it still shows the requested amount, and captured_money shows what was collected. On a standalone payment intent, PATCH can change it only before the first confirmation attempt.

authorization_expires_at.description: Deadline to capture a manual-capture hold. The authorization lapses at this time, and a capture attempted after it fails even if status is still requires_capture. Set when the hold is placed.

authorized_at.description: When the processor authorized the payment. Absent until then.

authorized_money.description: The amount the processor authorized. It always equals amount_money and doesn't change once set. Absent until the payment is authorized, and on payments canceled before authorization.

cancellation_reason.description: Flint-normalized reason the payment intent was canceled. Present only while status is canceled. Unknown processor values are returned as payment_canceled.

capturable_money.description: The part of the authorization you can still capture. Positive only while status is requires_capture, and zero after you capture or cancel or the authorization expires. The authorization lapses at authorization_expires_at, and a capture attempted after that fails even if this is positive. Absent until the payment is authorized.

capture_method.description: When money is collected. Defaults to automatic.
x-enum-descriptions: The payment is collected when it is confirmed.
Confirming places a hold. Capture all or part of it, or cancel it, before authorization_expires_at.

captured_at.description: When money was captured. For automatic capture, this is when the payment succeeded. Absent until capture.

captured_money.description: The amount collected from the buyer. Reconcile revenue and print receipts from this amount, not amount_money. Zero while a hold is open, and positive whenever status is succeeded. processing_fee_money, merchant_net_money, and refunds are based on it. Absent until the payment is authorized.

checkout_session_id.description: Flint checkout session ID associated with this payment, when present.

customer.description: The linked customer. Returned only with expand=customer.

customer_id.description: Customer linked to this payment intent.

dispute_status.description: Dispute state of this payment. none means no dispute or inquiry is open or recorded. The inquiry_ values track an issuer inquiry or early warning that isn't a chargeback. Read the dispute with GET /v1/disputes for its deadline and evidence.
x-enum-descriptions: No dispute is recorded for this payment.
The issuer asked for information before any chargeback. Respond by evidence_due_at.
You responded to the inquiry and the issuer is reviewing it.
The inquiry closed without becoming a chargeback. Final.
A chargeback is open and needs your response by evidence_due_at.
Evidence was submitted and the bank is deciding.
Decided against you, or a bank return that could not be contested. Final.
Resolved before it became a chargeback. Final.
Flint received a dispute state it does not recognize yet. Not final. Treat the dispute as open, do not assume an outcome, and read it again later. A response session still opens.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

fulfillment_hold.description: Present when a payment provider asked Flint to pause fulfillment for this payment. While its status is active, open fulfillments on the order are on hold with reason payment_review. payment_intent.fulfillment_hold_updated is sent when the hold starts and when it lifts.

invoice.description: The linked invoice. Returned only with expand=invoice.

invoice_id.description: Invoice this payment intent collects, when it pays an invoice.

last_payment_error.description: Most recent payment error. Null when no payment error is recorded.

merchant_id.description: Merchant that owns this payment intent.

merchant_net_money.description: Captured amount minus processing_fee_money and every amount in add_on_fees. Later merchant assessments and credits are separate balance effects. Absent until Flint has determined and verified the fee. If Flint can't verify it when you read the payment intent, the field is omitted rather than shown unverified; read the payment intent again later.

metadata.description: Caller-owned metadata. Keys starting with flint_ are reserved for Flint and aren't returned.

order.description: The linked order. Returned only with expand=order.

order_id.description: Order this payment intent belongs to. Create it through the order and confirm it with POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay. Capture and cancel use POST /v1/payment-intents/{payment_intent_id}/capture or /cancel for every payment intent. Order-owned intents accept PATCH for metadata and external_reference_id.

payment_flow.description: How the payment was started. Fixed when the payment intent is created.
x-enum-descriptions: Started in a Flint checkout session.
The first payment of a subscription.
Entered in the Dashboard virtual terminal.
Created by your integration through the API.

payment_intent_id.description: Flint payment intent ID.

payment_options.description: Payment options the buyer can use for this payment.

payment_source.description: Summary of the card or bank account used for the payment. Absent until a payment source is attached.

processing_fee_money.description: Flint's all-in processing fee for this payment. It is the complete price Flint charges to process the payment, never a provider cost passed through. The fee is final once the card payment is captured or the ACH payment succeeds; canceled payments and failures before success have none. Invoice, subscription, and automatic tax fees are itemized separately in add_on_fees. Your net for the payment is captured_money minus this fee and the add-on fees. Refunds do not return or revise it. Absent until Flint has determined and verified the fee. If Flint can't verify it when you read the payment intent, the field is omitted rather than shown unverified; read the payment intent again later.

receipt_email.description: Email address for this payment's receipt. When it isn't set, Flint uses the customer's email.

refund_status.description: How much of captured_money has been refunded, including value issued as store credit, based on refunded_money.
x-enum-descriptions: Part of captured_money has been refunded.
All of captured_money has been refunded.

refunded_money.description: Total refunded against captured_money, including value issued as store credit and processor refunds still pending. Failed and canceled refunds aren't counted. Zero when nothing has been refunded.

released_money.description: The part of the authorization returned to the buyer without being charged: the uncaptured remainder after a partial capture, or the whole authorization after a cancellation or expiry. It was never collected, so it needs no refund and can't be captured later. Absent until the payment is authorized.

return_id.description: Flint return ID associated with this payment, when present.

risk.description: Risk assessment. Always present with merchant credentials; null when no risk assessment is available. Omitted with the checkout credential.

selected_payment_option.description: The payment option the most recent confirmation used. Absent until the payment intent is first confirmed.

support_reference.description: Opaque payment reference to share with merchant support. Do not parse its format.

supported_actions.description: Actions the payment intent's current state accepts, each a POST to /v1/payment-intents/{payment_intent_id}/{action}. An action that isn't listed returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED. A listed action can still be refused because of something outside the payment intent: an open risk review, an order payment attempt that is using this payment, a closed order, or the merchant's account. An order-owned payment intent never lists confirm; pay it with POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay. The list changes only when the payment intent changes. Always empty for buyer credentials. New actions may be added.

tip_money.description: Portion of amount_money that is a tip. Uses amount_money's currency and is at most amount_money.

transaction_purpose.description: Why a bank debit is taken. Set only when payment_options includes ach_debit, and fixed once the payment intent exists.

version.description: Persisted version of this resource's owned state. Expanded resources and external observations can change independently.

The confirm result's current_payment_action describes a standalone payment's step; call confirm with an empty body to retrieve it again. Afterward, call confirm with an empty body, or resume the order's payment attempt.

Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly. A processing payment intent can't be canceled or updated.
A manual-capture hold is in place and no money has been collected. Capture up to capturable_money, or cancel, before authorization_expires_at.
Canceled before any money was collected, by you or by Flint, for example when an invoice is voided. Final. cancellation_reason says why when Flint knows it. A canceled hold is in released_money.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final.
A manual-capture hold reached authorization_expires_at without a capture, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. The payment_intent.expired event reports it; cancellation_reason is absent.

current_payment_action.description: Typed browser authority for the current standalone payment action. Complete it, then call the same confirm endpoint with an empty body. Null when no buyer action is needed or Flint cannot produce the action yet. If status is requires_action and this is null, call confirm again with an empty body.

PaymentIntentWithAction.description: One payment from a buyer, standalone or as a leg of an order. amount_money is the amount requested. Once the payment is authorized, authorized_money equals amount_money and splits into captured_money (collected), capturable_money (still on hold), and released_money (returned without being charged), so authorized_money always equals the sum of those three. Reconcile revenue from captured_money.

payment_collection.description: Setup details your client uses to collect the buyer's payment details. Required on both standalone and order-owned creates. On GET, returned only for a standalone intent in requires_payment_method or requires_confirmation, and omitted for an intent owned by a checkout session when read with merchant credentials. Order-owned intents never include it on GET; use Order.payment_collection, whose selectable_payment_intents lists the staged payments.

PaymentIntentWithCollection.description: One payment from a buyer, standalone or as a leg of an order. amount_money is the amount requested. Once the payment is authorized, authorized_money equals amount_money and splits into captured_money (collected), capturable_money (still on hold), and released_money (returned without being charged), so authorized_money always equals the sum of those three. Reconcile revenue from captured_money.

PaymentLimitSettings.description: Optional merchant limits that can lower Flint's payment-option and surface policy limits.

max_amounts.description: Map replaced as a whole: the keys you send become the full map. Maximum USD amounts keyed by default, surface, or an exact payment_option.surface selector. Merchant settings cannot raise Flint's policy ceiling.

min_amounts.description: Map replaced as a whole: the keys you send become the full map. Minimum USD amounts keyed by default, surface, or an exact payment_option.surface selector. Merchant settings cannot lower Flint's payment-option floor.

PaymentLimitSettingsPatch.description: Changes to a merchant's payment amount limits. Each map replaces the existing one, and null clears it.

max_amounts.description: Map replaced as a whole: the keys you send become the full map. Replaces this merchant limit map. Keys are default, a surface, payment_option.default, or payment_option.surface. Amounts must satisfy Flint's existing selector bounds and effective minimum/maximum range. Send null to clear this map; reads then omit it.

min_amounts.description: Map replaced as a whole: the keys you send become the full map. Replaces this merchant limit map. Keys are default, a surface, payment_option.default, or payment_option.surface. Amounts must satisfy Flint's existing selector bounds and effective minimum/maximum range. Send null to clear this map; reads then omit it.

PaymentLink.description: A reusable link that opens checkout.

buyer_fields.description: What checkout asks the buyer for. Each field you leave out uses your checkout settings.

checkout_session_expires_in_seconds.description: Seconds each checkout session the link starts stays open, from 60 to 86,400. Omit it to use your checkout settings, or 24 hours. It doesn't end the link; use sales_end_at for that.

delivery_method_ids.description: Delivery methods the link offers. Empty when the link has none, and then its checkouts offer settings.checkout.default_delivery_method_ids when the order has items to deliver.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

redirects.description: Where checkout sessions started from this payment link send the buyer after payment, cancellation, or expiration.

sales_end_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp after which the link stops starting checkouts and resolve returns PAYMENT_LINK_SALES_ENDED. Unset means sales do not end on their own, except that an event link without sales_end_at stops selling at event_config.event_at. A checkout opened before the end can still start payment for up to 15 minutes after it.

sales_summary.description: Present only with expand=sales_summary on GET /v1/payment-links or GET /v1/payment-links/{payment_link_id}. Available to merchant callers, including dashboard sessions and API keys with checkouts.payment_links.read. Uses the same paid-order definition as the merchant sales summary.

total_quantity_sold.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

PaymentLinkCustomField.description: A custom field on a payment link that collects an answer from the buyer, such as text, a dropdown, or a checkbox.

key.description: Unique custom field key. Must not have leading or trailing whitespace. Buyer answers are stored in order metadata as custom_field_<key>.

max_length.description: Maximum answer length for text and textarea fields, counted in Unicode code points. Defaults to 255 for text and 1000 for textarea when omitted. Each code point can occupy up to four UTF-8 bytes in the combined metadata size budget.

options.description: Dropdown choices. Dropdown fields require at least one option. Options must not have leading or trailing whitespace. The longest option in UTF-8 bytes counts toward the combined metadata size budget.

PaymentLinkCustomFieldInput.description: A custom field you add to a payment link when creating it.

key.description: Unique custom field key. Must not have leading or trailing whitespace. Buyer answers are stored in order metadata as custom_field_<key>.

max_length.description: Maximum answer length for text and textarea fields, counted in Unicode code points. Defaults to 255 for text and 1000 for textarea when omitted. Each code point can occupy up to four UTF-8 bytes in the combined metadata size budget.

options.description: Dropdown choices. Dropdown fields require at least one option. Options must not have leading or trailing whitespace. The longest option in UTF-8 bytes counts toward the combined metadata size budget.

PaymentLinkCustomFieldPatchInput.description: A custom field in a payment link update. Include its ID to change an existing field, or omit the ID to add a new one.

key.description: Unique custom field key. Must not have leading or trailing whitespace. Buyer answers are stored in order metadata as custom_field_<key>.

max_length.description: Maximum answer length for text and textarea fields, counted in Unicode code points. Defaults to 255 for text and 1000 for textarea when omitted. Each code point can occupy up to four UTF-8 bytes in the combined metadata size budget.

options.description: Dropdown choices. Dropdown fields require at least one option. Options must not have leading or trailing whitespace. The longest option in UTF-8 bytes counts toward the combined metadata size budget.

payment_link_custom_field_id.description: Stable ID of an existing custom field. Omit it to create a new custom field.

PaymentLinkCustomTextConfig.description: Custom text shown on a payment link's checkout, such as the order summary message and shipping address label.

PaymentLinkCustomTextPatchInput.description: Changes to a payment link's custom checkout text. Send null to clear a field.

PaymentLinkEventConfig.description: Event settings on an event payment link, such as its date, venue, ticket limit, and ticket emails.

max_total_quantity.description: Most tickets the event sells across all orders. Absent means no limit. On update, send null to remove the limit; a value below the tickets already sold or held by payments in progress returns MAX_TOTAL_QUANTITY_BELOW_SOLD. Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

ticket_prefix.description: Prefix for ticket numbers, up to 5 characters. It cannot change after the event has issued tickets.

PaymentLinkEventConfigInput.description: Event settings you supply when creating an event payment link.

max_total_quantity.description: Most tickets the event sells across all orders. Absent means no limit. On update, send null to remove the limit; a value below the tickets already sold or held by payments in progress returns MAX_TOTAL_QUANTITY_BELOW_SOLD. Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

ticket_prefix.description: Prefix for ticket numbers, up to 5 characters. It cannot change after the event has issued tickets.

PaymentLinkEventConfigPatchInput.description: Changes to an event payment link's settings. Send null on a nullable field to clear it.

max_total_quantity.description: Most tickets the event sells across all orders. Absent means no limit. On update, send null to remove the limit; a value below the tickets already sold or held by payments in progress returns MAX_TOTAL_QUANTITY_BELOW_SOLD. Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

ticket_prefix.description: Prefix for ticket numbers, up to 5 characters. It cannot change after the event has issued tickets. Send null to clear it.

PaymentLinkLegalConfig.description: Legal links on a payment link: contract, refund policy, shipping policy, and terms of service URLs, and whether buyers must accept the terms.

PaymentLinkLegalPatchInput.description: Changes to a payment link's legal links and terms setting. Send null on a URL to clear it.

PaymentLinkLineItem.description: A line item on a payment link, sold from a catalog variant, a bundle, or an ad hoc name and price, with quantity and price rules.

is_catalog_item_unavailable.description: True when this line item references a variant or bundle that is missing, deleted, or inactive, so it cannot be sold right now. Always false on ad-hoc line items.

key.description: Keys the resolve override maps. Stable line item key used in checkout overrides. Must not have leading or trailing whitespace. Assigned as line_item_1, line_item_2, and so on when omitted, skipping numbers already used by explicit keys; retained for an existing line item when omitted on update.

max_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

min_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

resolved_name.description: Current catalog name of the referenced variant or bundle. A variant reads as the product name, plus the variant name when the variant is a named option combination. This is the catalog value at read time, not a stored snapshot: checkout resolves it again when a buyer opens the link. Absent on ad-hoc line items and when the catalog object no longer exists.

resolved_unit_price_money.description: Current catalog unit price of the referenced variant or bundle. This is the catalog value at read time, not a stored snapshot: checkout resolves the price again when a buyer opens the link, so the amount a buyer pays can differ. Absent on ad-hoc line items and when the catalog object no longer exists.

PaymentLinkLineItemInput.description: A line item you add to a payment link when creating it, from a catalog variant, a bundle, or an ad hoc name and price.

key.description: Keys the resolve override maps. Stable line item key used in checkout overrides. Must not have leading or trailing whitespace. Assigned as line_item_1, line_item_2, and so on when omitted, skipping numbers already used by explicit keys; retained for an existing line item when omitted on update.

max_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

min_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

quantity.description: Whole-number default quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. Omission uses 1. Must be at least 1 for standard links; event tiers also accept 0.

PaymentLinkLineItemPatchInput.description: A line item in a payment link update. Include its ID to change an existing line item, or omit the ID to add a new one.

key.description: Keys the resolve override maps. Stable line item key used in checkout overrides. Must not have leading or trailing whitespace. Assigned as line_item_1, line_item_2, and so on when omitted, skipping numbers already used by explicit keys; retained for an existing line item when omitted on update.

max_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

min_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

payment_link_line_item_id.description: Stable ID of an existing line item. Omit it to create a new line item.

quantity.description: Whole-number default quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. Omission uses 1. Must be at least 1 for standard links; event tiers also accept 0.

PaymentLinkPaymentConfig.description: Payment settings on a payment link: the enabled payment options and a note shown with payment.

PaymentLinkPaymentPatchInput.description: Changes to a payment link's payment settings. Send null on the payment note to clear it.

PaymentLinkRedirectsPatchInput.description: Changes to a payment link's hosted checkout destinations. Omit a URL to leave it unchanged, or send null to clear it.

cancel_url.description: Where the buyer goes when they leave checkout without paying. The session stays open until it expires. Absolute HTTPS URL; test mode also accepts HTTP loopback URLs. Up to 2,048 characters. Send null to clear it.

expired_url.description: Where Flint sends a buyer who opens the session after it expires. Without it, the buyer sees Flint's expired-checkout page. Absolute HTTPS URL; test mode also accepts HTTP loopback URLs. Up to 2,048 characters. Send null to clear it.

success_url.description: Where the buyer goes after paying. Flint adds checkout_session_id and order_id query parameters, replacing any with those names. The redirect doesn't prove payment: confirm with the order.paid webhook or by reading the session. Absolute HTTPS URL; test mode also accepts HTTP loopback URLs. Up to 2,048 characters. Send null to clear it.

PaymentLinkSalesSummary.description: Paid-order sales totals for a payment link, computed on request. Paid means the order's collection has completed. Fully and partially refunded orders still count, and paid_totals reports the amount collected before refunds. Each order counts once even if it has multiple checkout sessions.

computed_at.description: UTC time at which the summary was computed, at second precision.

paid_order_count.description: Number of orders whose collection has completed, across all currencies, including fully and partially refunded orders.

paid_totals.description: Gross paid totals in integer minor units, one Money object per currency with paid orders, sorted by currency. Refunds are not subtracted. Empty array when there are no paid orders.

refunded_totals.description: Refunded totals in integer minor units on the same paid orders as paid_totals. One Money object per currency with paid orders, sorted by currency, including zero when nothing was refunded. Empty array when there are no paid orders.

PaymentLinkSubscriptionPreview.description: Subscription terms shown before an active plan-backed payment link creates a checkout session.

billing_interval_count.description: Number of billing intervals between recurring charges.

billing_interval_options.description: Billing intervals the plan offers, which the buyer chooses among on the checkout this link opens. The same values as the subscription plan's `billing_interval_options`.

contract_term_months.description: The term agreed with the buyer, in months, when configured. Flint records it on the subscription and does not stop the buyer from canceling earlier.

delivery_required.description: True when the plan has a line that ships or is delivered, so each renewal adds a shipping or delivery charge chosen at checkout. The amount is not known until the buyer enters an address and chooses a method.

early_termination_fee_money.description: The fee agreed for canceling before the recorded term ends, when configured. Flint records it on the subscription but never charges it.

plan_image.description: Plan image shown to the buyer, when configured.

plan_name.description: Plan name shown to the buyer.

quantity_options.description: Quantities the plan offers, which the buyer chooses among on the checkout this link opens. The same values as the subscription plan's `quantity_options`.

recurring_total_money.description: Recurring total for one billing interval, including line quantities and resolved modifiers.

setup_fee_money.description: Setup fee added to the first amount due, when configured.

trial_period_days.description: Number of trial days before the first recurring charge, when configured.

PaymentLinkThemeConfig.description: Theme settings for a payment link's checkout: accent color, primary color, and title.

PaymentLinkThemePatchInput.description: Changes to a payment link's checkout theme. Send null on a field to clear it.

fingerprint.description: A value that is the same for every saved copy of one card number at this merchant and environment, so you can spot duplicates. It doesn't identify the card anywhere else. A card added through Apple Pay or Google Pay can have a different fingerprint from the same card typed in.

is_default.description: Whether this is the customer's default payment method, the one Customer.default_payment_method_id names. Change the default with PATCH /v1/customers/{customer_id}; that sends customer.updated, not a payment method event.

saved_with.description: Where the buyer saved this payment method. Returned on /v1/me/payment-methods responses when Flint wallet support is enabled. Accept future values.

usage.description: When Flint may charge the payment method. off_session payment methods can pay subscriptions, automatic invoices, and other charges without the buyer, and can be a customer's default. on_session payment methods were saved by the buyer in checkout for faster checkout at this merchant; Flint charges them only in checkouts the buyer completes and refuses them for any charge without the buyer and as a default. Payment methods saved before usage existed are off_session.

PaymentMethodDomain.description: A domain registered for browser payment methods.

payment_option_statuses.description: Availability and validation status of each payment option on this domain.

version.description: Persisted version of this resource's owned state. Expanded resources and external observations can change independently.

PaymentMethodDomainPaymentOptionStatus.description: Whether a wallet payment option, Apple Pay or Google Pay, is active, inactive, or unavailable for a payment method domain.

client_setup.description: Present when the buyer must complete processor setup before using this payment method.

PaymentMethodWithSetup.description: The saved payment method, with `client_setup` when the buyer must still complete processor setup before the payment method can be used.

PaymentRefund.description: The part of a refund returned through one payment, with the amount, tip, status, and any failure reason.

failure_reason.description: Why a refund failed or a payment refund was canceled. Failed and canceled amounts become refundable again. Fix the cause, then create a new refund with a new idempotency key. Unknown provider values are returned as refund_failed.
x-enum-descriptions: The card can no longer receive credits.
The card was reported lost or stolen.
The refund could not be funded.
Your available balance could not cover the refund.
The card issuer declined the credit.
The refund was stopped at the merchant's request.
The payment is under dispute, or a bank return took the money back first. The buyer already has it through their bank.
On partially_succeeded: one or more payment refunds failed. Read payment_refunds.
This payment refund was canceled before it was attempted because another payment refund failed.
The refund failed with no more specific reason.

status.description: Status of this payment refund or tender allocation. A succeeded refund can still fail after a bank rejection. Parent status transitions send refund.succeeded, refund.partially_succeeded, or refund.failed; other public changes send refund.updated.
x-enum-descriptions: The payment method needs more information before the refund can finish. The parent refund stays pending.
The processor accepted the refund. A bank can still reject it later.
Not attempted because another payment refund in the same refund failed first. failure_reason is payment_refund_not_attempted.

PaymentReview.description: A payment review requiring a merchant decision.

closed_by.description: The credential that closed this payment review. Null when Flint closed it.

x-enum-descriptions: You declined the payment. Flint canceled the authorization, or refunded it when `refund_id` is set.
The payment was refunded in full outside the review.
A dispute opened on the payment.
The payment was canceled outside the review.
The authorization expired before a decision.

last_resolution_failure.description: The most recent resolution attempt that failed. Set when a decline's refund failed and the review reopened. Null when no attempt has failed.

refund_id.description: The refund that closed this review. Null otherwise.

refunded_money.description: Refunded amount for this review. Null when no refund is recorded.

resolution_started_by.description: The credential that started resolving this payment review. Null when Flint started it.

PaymentReviewPaymentSummary.description: The payment details shown on a review: amount, capture method, authorization expiry, card brand and last four digits, and buyer email.

PaymentReviewResolutionFailure.description: A failed attempt to resolve a review by refund, with the `refund_id` and when it failed.

PaymentReviewRisk.description: The risk assessment shown on a review: a `level` and, when available, a numeric `score`.

x-enum-descriptions: The card processor's fraud screening found nothing unusual.
The screening found signs of higher fraud risk.
The screening found strong signs of fraud.
No screening result, for example because Flint blocked the payment before authorization or the payment method isn't screened.

score.description: Fraud score from the card processor's screening, from 0 to 99. Higher means riskier. Absent when no score is available, which isn't a score of 0.

PaymentRisk.description: The risk assessment for a payment intent, with its risk level, score, outcome, and any matched rule or review.

x-enum-descriptions: The card processor's fraud screening found nothing unusual.
The screening found signs of higher fraud risk.
The screening found strong signs of fraud.
No screening result, for example because Flint blocked the payment before authorization or the payment method isn't screened.

score.description: Fraud score from the card processor's screening, from 0 to 99. Higher means riskier. Absent when no score is available, which isn't a score of 0.

PaymentSourceAchDebitSummary.description: Display details for a bank account payment source: account type, bank name, and last four digits.

PaymentSourceCardSummary.description: Display details for a card payment source: brand, last four digits, and payment method ID.

PaymentSourceCredential.description: The credential you provide to pay an order: a payment source token, a saved payment method ID, or a Stripe confirmation token.

token.description: Opaque processor or browser payment source token.

payment_method_id.description: Saved Flint payment method ID belonging to the customer making this payment.

stripe.description: Stripe credential collected for this payment.

confirmation_token.description: Stripe confirmation token you created with Stripe.js from `payment_collection.stripe`.

PaymentSourceSummary.description: A summary of the payment source used for a payment, by funding-method family, with card or bank account display details.

type.description: Funding-method family. Wallet payment options use card because their underlying funding source is a card.

PaymentVolumeBucket.description: The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

payments_count.description: Succeeded payments selected by payment created_at within this bucket, restricted to the response currency. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

period_end_at.description: Exclusive bucket end instant, clipped to the resolved period. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

period_start_at.description: Inclusive start instant. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

volume_money.description: Succeeded payment amounts selected by payment created_at within this bucket, in the response currency. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

PaymentVolumeTimeseries.description: The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

buckets.description: Payment created_at buckets clipped to the period, including empty buckets. Repeated local hours produce two buckets; skipped hours and days produce none. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

currencies.description: Currencies of succeeded payments selected by payment created_at or counted refunds selected by refund created_at in the period, regardless of the currency filter. Empty when neither has rows. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency for amounts and payment counts. Defaults to the merchant's default currency. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

granularity.description: Local bucket size: hour, day, week starting Monday, or month. Defaults to day. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

period_end_at.description: Exclusive resolved end instant. Omitted or future request ends resolve to the request time truncated to the second. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

period_start_at.description: Inclusive start instant. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used only for local bucket boundaries. Defaults to UTC. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

Payout.description: Funds sent from a merchant balance to a payout destination.

amount_money.description: Amount sent to your bank. Always positive.

arrival_date.description: Calendar date the bank is expected to receive the funds, in YYYY-MM-DD format using the UTC date of the expected arrival.

balance_source_type.description: Balance source this payout draws from. Flint chooses the source when balance_source_type is omitted at create. Clients must accept source types added in future releases.

description.description: Description sent when the payout was created. Absent when there is none.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

failure_code.description: Flint-normalized payout failure code. Unknown provider values are returned as payout_failed.

failure_message.description: Flint-authored payout failure message. This is stable explanatory text, not a raw provider message.

fee_amount_status.description: Whether the payout fee is estimated or final. not_applicable means no applicable fee status is known, including unmapped fee states.

fee_money.description: Fee for this payout, never negative. Payouts carry no fee, so this is 0 once your processor records the payout, and null until then.

initiated_by.description: What started the payout. A payout imported from your processor follows the processor: scheduled when it sent the payout automatically, otherwise manual. Only scheduled payouts list their balance transactions through GET /v1/balance-transactions?payout_id=; other payouts return 409 with reason not_itemized. Unmapped sources are returned as other.
x-enum-descriptions: Created through the API or dashboard.
Created by the merchant's payout schedule.
Created by Flint on the merchant's behalf.
An unmapped source started the payout.

metadata.description: Caller-owned metadata. Values can't be empty strings. Keys starting with flint_ are reserved for Flint, are not returned, and cannot be written through the public API.

method.description: Payout method. instant can appear on imported payouts; unmapped methods are returned as other.

net_money.description: Signed effect of this payout on your Flint balance. It is negative because the payout takes money out: a 25000 payout with no fee has net_money -25000. Null until your processor records the payout.

original_payout.description: The payout this one reverses, inlined when you request expand=original_payout. null when expanded and original_payout_id is absent.

original_payout_id.description: On a payout that reverses another payout, the payout it reverses. A payout has at most one of original_payout_id and reversed_by_payout_id.

payout_destination.description: The payout destination, inlined when you request expand=payout_destination. null when expanded and payout_destination_id is absent.

payout_destination_id.description: Bank account or debit card receiving the payout. Absent when Flint can't match your processor's destination to a payout destination.

reversal_status.description: Whether Flint has pulled a paid payout back from your bank: none, reversing while a reversal is in progress, or reversed once it completes and a payout_reversal balance transaction returns the money. status stays paid throughout.

reversed_by_payout.description: The payout that reversed this one, inlined when you request expand=reversed_by_payout. null when expanded and reversed_by_payout_id is absent.

reversed_by_payout_id.description: On a reversed payout, the separate payout that reversed it, when there is one. A payout has at most one of original_payout_id and reversed_by_payout_id.

statement_descriptor.description: Text shown on your bank statement for the deposit, when one was set.

status.description: Where the payout is: pending until it is sent, in_transit on its way to your bank, then paid or failed. A paid payout can still become failed if the bank returns the deposit, and canceled means a manual payout was canceled while pending.

trace_id.description: The bank's trace number for the deposit, which your bank can use to locate a late deposit. Its status says whether the number is pending, available, or unsupported, and value holds the number when Flint has it. Absent when Flint has no trace information.

PayoutDestination.description: The account that receives merchant payouts.

available_payout_methods.description: Payout methods available through Flint for this destination. Only standard is currently available.

bank_name.description: Name of the bank, when your processor reports it.

default_for_currency.description: Whether this is the default destination for its currency. Scheduled payouts, and payouts created without payout_destination_id, go to the default, and only an active destination can be it.

disabled_at.description: When the destination was last disabled or archived. Absent if it never was.

disabled_reason.description: Flint-normalized reason the payout destination cannot currently be used. Unknown provider/backend values are returned as destination_unavailable.

last4.description: Last four digits of the account or card number.

metadata.description: Caller-owned metadata. Values can't be empty strings. Keys starting with flint_ are reserved for Flint, are not returned, and cannot be written through the public API.

payout_destination_id.description: Stable identifier of the payout destination.

status.description: Current status. Archived: deleted, and still readable by ID.
x-enum-descriptions: Archived: deleted, and still readable by ID.

status_updated_at.description: When Flint last recorded the destination's status.

type.description: Destination type. Unmapped destination types are returned as other.

version.description: Persisted version of this resource's owned state. Expanded resources and external observations can change independently.

PayoutSettings.description: The merchant's payout schedule and preferences.

blocked_reasons.description: Why payouts can't run. Empty when nothing blocks them.

created_at.description: When Flint stored the payout settings record, as an RFC 3339 UTC instant at second precision. Null when no stored settings record exists.

default_payout_destinations.description: Default payout destination for each currency, as a map from currency code to payout_destination_id. Read-only: change defaults in the payouts embedded component.

PricingAmounts.description: The money totals for an order or invoice: subtotal, discounts, charges, tax, requested tip, and total.

additive_tax_money.description: Tax added on top of prices, included in total_money.

charge_money.description: Total of the order's service charges after service-charge discounts.

discount_money.description: Total of order and line-item discounts. Service-charge discounts, such as free shipping, are not included; they reduce charge_money.

inclusive_tax_money.description: Tax already included in subtotal_money and charge_money. Informational; it is not added again to total_money.

requested_tip_money.description: Tip money in the total: the requested tip before payment, and settled tips net of refunds after.

subtotal_money.description: Sum of the line items' subtotal_money: prices with modifiers, before discounts. Lines with tax-inclusive prices include their tax here.

tax_money.description: Total tax, equal to additive_tax_money + inclusive_tax_money.

total_money.description: subtotal_money - discount_money + charge_money + additive_tax_money + requested_tip_money, never below zero.

Promotion.description: Promotion evaluation order: manual discounts stay, do not count toward the cap, and are ignored by combines_with. Frozen subscription-term promotions are admitted first and are exempt from exclusivity, combines_with, and the cap. Candidates include codes being applied, existing promotion discounts, and qualifying automatic promotions. Each exclusivity group keeps its highest-priority member, then the larger standalone discount, earlier created_at, and lower promotion_id. Remaining candidates rank by standalone discount, then earlier created_at and lower promotion_id; each is admitted unless max_promotions_per_order is reached or both promotions do not allow each other's discount class. Admitted promotions price line item first, then order, then service charge. A zero-value promotion is dropped and selection runs again.

allocation.description: How the effect is applied across the matched items or charges. each applies the effect to every matched item independently: a fixed amount_off is charged per item (10 USD off 3 items discounts 30 USD, each capped at the item price), and a percent_off is taken from each item. across applies the effect once to the matched set as a whole: a fixed amount_off is the whole amount one time (10 USD off the group total, not prorated per item), and a percent_off is taken from the combined subtotal. For percent_off the two produce the same total and differ only in how the discount is attributed to individual line items; for amount_off they differ by the number of matched items, so set it deliberately. Defaults to each for line_item and service_charge promotions and across for order promotions. max_discounted_quantity requires each.

PromotionRule.description: One condition in a promotion rule group, which tests an attribute with an operator and values.

attribute.description: Field the rule tests. The attribute fixes the value type and the operators that are legal for it: money attributes accept comparison operators but not eq or in, booleans accept eq only, and so on. The full attribute/type/operator matrix is machine-readable in x-flint-rule-attributes on this schema. metadata.<key> reads a string from the customer's metadata and accepts the string operators. A disallowed operator is rejected at create time with INVALID_OPERATOR, whose message names the operators allowed for the attribute.

currency_options.description: Alternative thresholds for money-valued rules, keyed by currency code. Each Money currency must match its key.

operator.description: Comparison to apply to the attribute. The attribute determines which operators are allowed.

values.description: Comparison values with the type required by the attribute. Omit for is_defined, which tests whether the attribute is present.

PromotionRuleGroup.description: A rule group is an object with exactly one nonempty all (AND) or any (OR) array of rules or nested groups. Arrays, empty groups, and a rules key are invalid. Omit the field for no rules, or send null where the field is clearable. Responses list rules before nested groups. Under any, a nested group containing only one rule reads back as that rule. Under all, nested groups keep their boundaries to preserve matched_items.subtotal scope. These deterministic normalizations stabilize after one round trip. matched_items.subtotal sums the line items matched by the line_item.* rules in the same all group, including its nested groups.

all.description: Rules and nested groups that must all match.

any.description: Rules and nested groups of which at least one must match.

ReturnLineDecision.description: Start from the pinned policy proposal recomputed for approved_quantity when the line has a policy evaluation and the proposal can be built. Otherwise start with return_required_quantity equal to approved_quantity, allowed_resolution_types containing refund, exchange, replacement, no_monetary_action, and store_credit in that order regardless of whether the original payment is refundable, no automatic_resolution_type, is_inspection_required false, and no receiving_location_id. Each supplied field replaces its starting value; allowed_resolution_types replaces the whole list. Omit automatic_resolution_type to keep its starting value, or send null to resolve manually. Then fill an omitted release_timing with after_inspection when merchandise is required and inspection is required, after_receipt when merchandise is required without inspection, or after_approval when no merchandise is required. Validate the merged decision for quantity bounds, allowed resolution types, and reachable timing and inspection requirements. A pinned policy always requires override_reason when approved_quantity exceeds evaluated eligible_quantity, even when no proposal can be built. With a pinned policy but no proposal, other decision fields use these defaults and override_reason is otherwise optional.

allowed_resolution_types.description: Optional replacement for the entire starting list. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal; otherwise refund, exchange, replacement, no_monetary_action, and store_credit in that order, independent of the original payment's refundability. The resulting list must be valid and non-empty when approved_quantity is above zero.

approved_quantity.description: Required whole-number quantity from zero through the line's requested_quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. When approved_quantity is below requested_quantity, send decline_reason; decline_reason_message is optional. Both decline fields are forbidden when all requested quantity is approved.

automatic_resolution_type.description: Optional refund, store_credit, or no_monetary_action that Flint creates and confirms automatically. Omit to keep the policy proposal's value, or the absent value from no-policy defaults. Send null to resolve the line manually; clearing a policy proposal's automatic value requires override_reason. Must be in the resulting allowed_resolution_types. Exchange and replacement cannot be automated. An unavailable automatic refund or store credit fails with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason refund_unavailable or store_credit_unavailable.

is_inspection_required.description: Optional inspection requirement. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal or false when no proposal can be built. The resulting requirement must be reachable with the merged merchandise quantity and release timing.

override_reason.description: Required when a decision differs from a buildable pinned policy proposal. With a pinned policy, also required whenever approved_quantity exceeds evaluated eligible_quantity, even when no proposal can be built. The release timing fill also applies to the proposal and does not count as a deviation. Otherwise optional when a pinned policy proposal cannot be built or no deviation exists. Forbidden without a pinned policy.

override_reason_message.description: Optional explanation accompanying override_reason. Requires override_reason and is forbidden without a pinned policy.

release_timing.description: Optional gate for every resolution type. Defaults to the policy proposal's timing when set. ReturnProcessDecision.description: Start from the pinned policy proposal recomputed for approved_quantity when the line has a policy evaluation and the proposal can be built. Otherwise start with return_required_quantity equal to approved_quantity, allowed_resolution_types containing refund, exchange, replacement, no_monetary_action, and store_credit in that order regardless of whether the original payment is refundable, no automatic_resolution_type, is_inspection_required false, and no receiving_location_id. Each supplied field replaces its starting value; allowed_resolution_types replaces the whole list. Omit automatic_resolution_type to keep its starting value, or send null to resolve manually. Then fill an omitted release_timing with after_inspection when merchandise is required and inspection is required, after_receipt when merchandise is required without inspection, or after_approval when no merchandise is required. Validate the merged decision for quantity bounds, allowed resolution types, and reachable timing and inspection requirements. A pinned policy always requires override_reason when approved_quantity exceeds evaluated eligible_quantity, even when no proposal can be built. With a pinned policy but no proposal, other decision fields use these defaults and override_reason is otherwise optional.

allowed_resolution_types.description: Optional replacement for the entire starting list. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal; otherwise refund, exchange, replacement, no_monetary_action, and store_credit in that order, independent of the original payment's refundability. The resulting list must be valid and non-empty when approved_quantity is above zero.

approved_quantity.description: Required whole-number quantity from zero through the line's requested_quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. When approved_quantity is below requested_quantity, send decline_reason; decline_reason_message is optional. Both decline fields are forbidden when all requested quantity is approved.

automatic_resolution_type.description: Optional refund, store_credit, or no_monetary_action that Flint creates and confirms automatically. Omit to keep the policy proposal's value, or the absent value from no-policy defaults. Send null to resolve the line manually; clearing a policy proposal's automatic value requires override_reason. Must be in the resulting allowed_resolution_types. Exchange and replacement cannot be automated. An unavailable automatic refund or store credit fails with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason refund_unavailable or store_credit_unavailable.
x-enum-descriptions: Money back to the original payment, with gift card value sent to the chosen gift card destination.
Refunds the returned value onto new gift cards instead of the original payment. Card, wallet and Link payments and gift cards qualify; Affirm and ACH debit payments do not.

decline_reason_message.description: Optional explanation accompanying decline_reason, up to 2048 characters (Unicode code points), counted before normalization. Requires decline_reason and is forbidden when all requested quantity is approved.

is_inspection_required.description: Optional inspection requirement. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal or false when no proposal can be built. The resulting requirement must be reachable with the merged merchandise quantity and release timing.

override_reason.description: Required when a decision differs from a buildable pinned policy proposal. With a pinned policy, also required whenever approved_quantity exceeds evaluated eligible_quantity, even when no proposal can be built. The release timing fill also applies to the proposal and does not count as a deviation. Otherwise optional when a pinned policy proposal cannot be built or no deviation exists. Forbidden without a pinned policy.

override_reason_message.description: Optional explanation accompanying override_reason. Requires override_reason and is forbidden without a pinned policy.

receiving_location_id.description: Optional receiving Location with a postal address. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal or no location when no proposal can be built. Required when the resulting return_required_quantity is above zero and there is no starting location. A process receipt does not supply the decision's location.

release_timing.description: Optional gate for every resolution type. Defaults to the policy proposal's timing when set. After merging supplied fields, an unset timing becomes after_inspection when return_required_quantity is above zero and inspection is required, after_receipt when return_required_quantity is above zero without inspection, or after_approval when return_required_quantity is zero. Applies to every resolution type, including exchanges and replacements. manual is held until a merchant calls POST /v1/return-resolutions/{id}/release.

Capturing doesn't change it: after a partial capture it still shows the requested amount, and captured_money shows what was collected. On a standalone payment intent, PATCH can change it only before the first confirmation attempt.

last_payment_error.description: Most recent payment failure, when one is recorded.

payment_intent_id.description: Flint payment intent ID.

status.description: Lifecycle status. requires_payment_method covers both a new payment intent and one whose last attempt failed, so read last_payment_error with it. succeeded, canceled, and expired are final. Refunds and disputes never change status.
x-enum-descriptions: Waiting for the buyer's payment details. Either nothing has been attempted yet, or the last attempt was declined, failed, or blocked and last_payment_error says why. Confirm again with a new credential.

Payment details are attached, but confirmation hasn't finished. Flint usually confirms in the same request that attaches them, so this status is brief unless that confirmation was interrupted. Resume the order's payment attempt, or call confirm with an empty body for a standalone payment intent. The payment_intent.updated event reports changes into this status.

The buyer must finish a step, such as 3D Secure authentication or a redirect, before the payment can continue. The confirm result's current_payment_action describes a standalone payment's step; call confirm with an empty body to retrieve it again. Afterward, call confirm with an empty body, or resume the order's payment attempt.

Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly. A processing payment intent can't be canceled or updated.
A manual-capture hold is in place and no money has been collected. Capture up to capturable_money, or cancel, before authorization_expires_at.
Canceled before any money was collected, by you or by Flint, for example when an invoice is voided. Final. cancellation_reason says why when Flint knows it. A canceled hold is in released_money.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final.
A manual-capture hold reached authorization_expires_at without a capture, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. The payment_intent.expired event reports it; cancellation_reason is absent.

status.description:
Read-only shipment state derived from the shipment's package states. An empty shipment remains a created draft.
- `created`: The shipment leg exists but has not been packed or handed off.
- `packed`: The shipment leg is packed and awaiting carrier handoff.
- `shipped`: The shipment leg was handed to the carrier.
- `in_transit`: The carrier is moving the shipment through its network.
- `out_for_delivery`: The shipment is on its final delivery route.
- `delivered`: The carrier reported successful delivery.
- `delivery_attempted`: The carrier attempted delivery but did not complete it. Follow the carrier instructions before retrying delivery.
- `exception`: A carrier exception is blocking normal progress. Resolve the carrier-reported issue.
- `returned`: The shipment was returned toward or to its origin.
- `voided`: The shipment was voided and will not continue through delivery.
