SubscribedLine.description: The subscription offer and billing interval an order line was bought under, with the recurring amount.

recurring_amount_money.description: Line amount for the first renewal, including modifiers and recurring discounts, before shipping and tax. Signup-only discounts are excluded.

SubscribedLineInput.description: Makes an order line a subscription purchase, with the subscription offer and billing interval.

subscription_offer_id.description: Active subscription offer for this catalog variant.

awaiting_billing_schedule.description: True while an active or trialing subscription on an external billing schedule has no next billing date.

billing_anchor_day.description: UTC day of the month used for monthly and yearly billing. Applies only to Flint-owned schedules.

billing_interval.description: How often the subscription bills now. Read with billing_interval_count: monthly with a count of 3 bills quarterly. A change applies from the next renewal that has not been paid; next_billing_at does not move.

billing_interval_count.description: Number of billing_interval units between charges. Changes with billing_interval.

billing_schedule_owner.description: Who supplies billing dates: flint advances the schedule after each paid renewal; external uses dates you supply. Change it with billing_schedule on PATCH /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}.

buyer_actions.description: What the buyer can do with the subscription, in this order: cancel, pause, resume, reactivate, update_payment_method, retry_payment, update_delivery, skip, update_billing_interval, update_quantity, swap_items, then renew, under the store's buyer policy. The available cancel and pause actions carry the choices they accept. A buyer's read or change through a customer session on /v1/me, or in Flint's buyer account, lists all twelve every time; a merchant read gets an empty list. update_payment_method is required while a payment is past due, due by next_retry_at when a retry is scheduled, and when the card expires before next_billing_at, due by then.

cancel_at_period_end.description: True when the subscription is scheduled to cancel at scheduled_cancel_at. Schedule with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/cancel; undo with PATCH and cancel_at_period_end false.

cancellation_details.description: Who asked to cancel, when, and why. Present once a cancellation is requested, whether it takes effect at the end of the billing period or right away. Omitted when no one asked, and removed when a scheduled cancellation is undone. See cancellation_reason for voluntary and payment-related cancellations.

cancellation_reason.description: Why the subscription is canceled or scheduled to cancel. Uses cancellation_details.requested_by when recorded, payment_failed for a canceled subscription without a requester, and other for a scheduled cancellation without a requester. Omitted otherwise.
x-enum-descriptions: Payment failed without a recorded cancellation request.
A cancellation is scheduled without a recorded requester.

contract_end_at.description: When the recorded contract term ends. Does not move when the subscription pauses or changes plan. Flint does not stop the buyer from canceling earlier.

contract_start_at.description: When the recorded contract term started. Does not move when the subscription pauses or changes plan.

delivery.description: Saved delivery preference with the current delivery method display. Write responses use the same display as GET: fixed shipping reflects the current method configuration, and quoted shipping shows the last paid shipping amount when available.

delivery_hold.description: Current delivery issue that blocks collection. Mutually exclusive with upcoming_delivery_hold.

early_termination_fee_money.description: The fee in the recorded contract terms. Present whenever those terms include a fee. It applies only to a cancellation before contract_end_at. Flint never charges it. Later plan changes do not change this fee.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

inventory_wait.description: Renewal waiting for stock. Included only in merchant responses and omitted from buyer responses.

last_payment_error.description: Latest renewal payment failure, present only while status is past_due and the latest payment failed. Buyer responses omit merchant remediation and sensitive decline signals.

line_items.description: What each renewal bills. Plan edits do not change it. Adding, changing or swapping a line takes that variant's current catalog price, which then stays until the line changes again.

missed_billing_at.description: The billing date whose payment failed, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Present only while status is past_due.

next_billing_at.description: When Flint next starts a scheduled renewal charge, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Present only while a trialing or active subscription has a billing date and isn't set to cancel at the end of its period. Absent when no renewal is scheduled: a paused subscription resumes at scheduled_resume_at, a past_due one reports the failed billing date in missed_billing_at and retries at next_retry_at, an incomplete one retries at next_retry_at, a scheduled start begins at starts_at, one set to cancel ends at scheduled_cancel_at, and an external schedule awaiting a date reports awaiting_billing_schedule.

next_retry_at.description: Recorded automatic payment retry time. Null when no retry time is available.

open_renewal_order_id.description: ID of the paid renewal order whose shipment has not been dispatched. It keeps its committed delivery destination after preference changes and cancellation. Absent when no such renewal order exists. Only renewal orders count; the signup order is not included.

outstanding_money.description: Unpaid balance of the failed renewal order, including tax, shipping and discounts, after payments and credits. Present only while status is past_due and a positive balance remains.

pause_reason.description: Why the subscription is paused: merchant for a pause made with your API key or dashboard, buyer for the buyer's own pause, delivery_action_required for a pause during or after a delivery hold, and payment_failed when renewal payment retries ran out and your dunning settings pause the subscription. Omitted when the subscription is not paused.

payment_method_id.description: The saved payment method renewals charge. Change it with PATCH.

promotions.description: Recurring promotions applying to the next charged cycle. Empty when none apply; signup-only and exhausted promotions are excluded.

quantity.description: How many of each line the subscription bills each period, as a whole number; fractional quantities are not supported. A change applies from the next renewal that has not been paid.

recurring_subtotal_money.description: What one billing period's items cost before discounts, shipping, and tax: each line's price with modifiers, times quantity. It changes when items, quantity, or the plan change; editing the plan doesn't change it. For the next charge, use a subscription preview in next_renewal mode.

resume_requested_at.description: When Flint accepted a pending resume request. Set only while paused with a resume Flint has not applied yet. Clears when Flint resumes the subscription or refuses the request.

scheduled_cancel_at.description: When the scheduled cancellation takes effect: trial_end_at while trialing, current_period_end_at while active, or next_retry_at while past_due. Null when cancel_at_period_end is false or no cancellation time is available.

scheduled_resume_at.description: When a pause with a length (pause_duration_cycles) resumes on its own: that many billing intervals after paused_at. Null when the subscription is not paused or the pause has no length, such as a pause until you resume it or the pause Flint starts when a delivery hold runs out.

service_location.description: Omitted for a checkout session credential that doesn't act for the customer the buyer verified.

starts_at.description: When a scheduled start's first billing period begins. Present only until that first payment succeeds.

x-enum-descriptions: In the free trial. Nothing has been charged.
Current. After a trial it is active while the first charge runs.
A charge failed and Flint is retrying, or waiting for a new payment method.
The first period's payment is being collected, or is held (see delivery_hold and inventory_wait). Don't provision yet.
Created with a scheduled start. Nothing is charged before starts_at. At starts_at Flint collects the first period; it becomes active once paid, or past_due if the payment fails.

subscription_plan_id.description: Subscription plan ID. Omitted when terms_type is subscription_offer.

supported_actions.description: Merchant actions allowed by the subscription's state. A route can still refuse a listed action for a transient reason, such as a renewal already in progress, with its own error.

x-enum-descriptions: Cancel immediately or schedule cancellation with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/cancel.
Resume a paused subscription with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/resume.
Skip the next renewal with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/skip-cycle.
Order the next renewal now with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/renew.
Retry a past-due payment with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/payment-retries.
Change a plan-backed subscription's plan with POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/change-plan.

terms_type.description: Terms come from the subscription plan in subscription_plan_id, or from subscription offers identified on each offer line by subscription_offer_id.
x-enum-descriptions: Terms come from the subscription plan in subscription_plan_id.
Terms come from subscription offers; each offer line carries subscription_offer_id. There is no subscription_plan_id.

upcoming_delivery_hold.description: Delivery issue forecast for the next renewal at renewal_at. Mutually exclusive with delivery_hold.

SubscriptionAddressVerification.description: The verification state of a subscription's delivery address: `verified`, `unverified`, `needs_review`, or `unverifiable`.

The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

period_end_at.description: Exclusive resolved end instant. Omitted or future request ends resolve to the request time truncated to the second. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

period_start_at.description: Inclusive start instant. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

snapshot_metrics.description: Current persisted subscription state at computation time, cached briefly. Independent of the requested period end. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

window_metrics.description: Subscription creation, cancellation, and payment success metrics selected within the requested period. The half-open period [period_start_at, period_end_at) includes its start and excludes its end. Amounts and payments_count use currency; customer and subscription counts span currencies.

starts_at.description: Future instant when the first billing period starts.

collection.description: How the invoice is collected. Send the invoice's collection object back unchanged, or a new one. merchant_default resolves again from invoice settings when the draft is written.

expected_version.description: Invoice version last read. Required when schedule_entries is present. Required when any of these fields is present: schedule_entries.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system. Use it as your sync key: it isn't printed on the invoice, and GET /v1/invoices filters on it by exact match. Send null to clear it.

footer.description: Fine print at the bottom of the invoice and PDF. Send null to clear it.

memo.description: Message to the customer, printed on the invoice and PDF. Send null to clear it.

Keys starting with flint_ are reserved for Flint, are not returned, and cannot be written through the public API.

payment_due.description: When the invoice is due. Send the invoice's payment_due object back unchanged, or a new one. Sending payment_terms captures the term's current revision again.

po_number.description: The buyer's purchase order number, printed on the invoice and PDF. Send null to clear it.

recipient_email.description: Where Flint emails the invoice and its reminders. Required at issue when delivery resolves to email, and when you schedule the issue. Send null to clear it.

reference.description: Your reference for the invoice, printed on the invoice and PDF. Put the buyer's purchase order number in po_number instead. Send null to clear it.

reminders_paused.description: Pauses (true) or resumes (false) the automatic reminder cadence. Accepted only on an open or partially paid invoice with a balance remaining, and only alone or with expected_version: every other field is draft-only. While paused, manual send-reminder calls still work, and invoice.overdue and invoice.late_fee_due still fire. On resume, reminder times that passed while paused do not fire. Sending the current value succeeds without changing the invoice.

remit_to_address.description: Where the buyer sends offline payments, printed on the invoice. Omit it to use the invoice settings remit-to address.

schedule_entries.description: Complete draft payment schedule with at most 14 entries. Validation errors identify the entry by index, such as schedule_entries[3].kind. Enum values are case-sensitive and must not contain surrounding whitespace. Omission preserves the current or default schedule; [] clears the authored schedule. Null is not accepted. On PATCH, include invoice_schedule_entry_id to retain an entry and expected_version to detect concurrent edits.

scheduled_issue_at.description: When Flint issues and delivers this draft, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in the future. A scheduled issue delivers by email, so the draft needs recipient_email. Clearing it cancels the scheduled issue. Send null to clear it.

service_date.description: The calendar date of the billed service, in YYYY-MM-DD format. The invoice and PDF print it as written, without timezone conversion. Send null to clear it.

Requires expected_version from the order and clears the delivery selection when terms change. Send null to clear subscription. Requires expected_version.

address.description: Complete replacement postal address, validated as on create. Requires coordinate in the same request, including null to clear it.

coordinate.description: Complete replacement coordinate. Send null to clear both coordinate and coordinate_source. A non-null value requires coordinate_source in the same request.

coordinate_source.description: Source of the coordinate sent in the same request. A non-null coordinate requires merchant_supplied or geocoded. Send null only with coordinate: null to clear both fields.

Weight.description: A weight value in grams, kilograms, ounces, or pounds, used in delivery profile configuration.

unit.description: Weight unit. Use gram, kilogram, ounce, or pound.

value.description: Weight measured in the specified unit.

WorkloadIdentity.description: A policy that grants API access to a workload authenticated by an external identity provider.

archived_at.description: Time the identity was archived. Omitted before archival.

claim_conditions.description: Bounded value array of top-level scalar claim conditions. Replaced as a whole on PATCH; [] clears it when the remaining policy is valid.

last_used_at.description: Most recent use. Omitted before the first use.

platform.description: Computed from the issuer. New platform values may be added.

sandbox_id.description: The sandbox containing this identity. Present only in test mode.

scopes.description: Complete scope set granted to this identity. Replaced as a whole on PATCH.

version.description: Positive concurrency version. Increases on policy and lifecycle changes.

WorkloadIdentityClaimCondition.description: A condition matching one top-level scalar claim in the workload's identity token.

claim.description: Literal top-level scalar claim name. Registered JWT claims are reserved.

WorkloadIdentityClaimConditionInput.description: A condition to match one top-level scalar claim in the workload's identity token. Omitted match defaults to exact.

claim.description: Literal top-level scalar claim name. Registered JWT claims are reserved.

WorkloadIdentityCreator.description: The user or credential that created a workload identity, identified by resource type and ID.

BearerAuth.bearerFormat: Flint API key, partner install token, or short-lived Flint session token
BearerAuth.description: Flint secret API key, CLI OAuth access token, installation-scoped partner token, or session token sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Route-specific partner access and scopes are declared by x-flint-partner-access and x-flint-partner-required-scopes. Secret API keys use the flint_live_ or flint_test_ prefix; keep ordinary secret keys server-side. The first-party docs playground uses a dedicated sandbox-only sample key exception.

CheckoutSessionBearer.description: The checkout credential from checkout_auth_token, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. It acts for one checkout session and its order. Accepted only by the operations that list it.

CustomerSessionBearer.description: The customer session secret (`flint_cses_...`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Accepted only by `/v1/me`. Keep it on your server: Flint has no browser credential, and your backend relays the buyer's account calls.

InvoiceAccessTokenBearer.description: Invoice access token from the invoice's public URL. Accepted only for that invoice's buyer detail, PDF, and checkout-session endpoints.

OnboardingSessionBearer.description: Short-lived onboarding token returned by POST /v1/onboarding/verify-email. The credential selects the environment; the onboarding session token acts in the merchant's default sandbox. Refresh stays bound to the launch token's sandbox. Live onboarding requires a live API key or live CLI login.

info.description: Flint's public /v1 API for payments, checkout, invoices, subscriptions, catalog, customers, returns, inventory, money movement, webhooks, and developer operations. Use live keys for production and sandbox-bound test keys for staging or sandbox workflows; keep ordinary secret API keys server-side. The first-party docs playground uses a dedicated sandbox-only sample key exception. A request body can be up to 1 MiB unless an operation documents a lower limit; a larger body returns 413 with the REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE error code.
info.title: Flint Public API

get.description: Returns high-level merchant analytics for the requested half-open period.

parameters.description: Inclusive period start as an RFC 3339 instant. The period is [period_start_at, period_end_at), at most 400 days, or 32 days for hour granularity.
parameters.name: period_start_at

parameters.description: Exclusive period end as an RFC 3339 instant. Omitted or future values resolve to the request time, truncated to the second.
parameters.name: period_end_at

parameters.description: ISO 4217 currency for every amount and payments_count. Defaults to the merchant's default currency. Customer and subscription counts span currencies. currencies lists the available currencies.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: API version for this request. Overrides merchant and partner app defaults.
parameters.name: Flint-Version

parameters.description: Your own ID for this request, such as a log or trace ID, 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters. Flint stores it as client_request_id on the request log. The X-Request-Id response header is Flint's request ID, not this value.
parameters.name: X-Request-Id

Flint-Merchant-Id.description: Flint merchant ID for the authenticated request context.

Flint-Mode.description: Payment mode for the authenticated request context.

Flint-Sandbox-Id.description: Flint sandbox ID for authenticated test-mode requests when the request is sandbox-bound.

Flint-Version.description: API version used to encode this response. A replay can be served at an older version than requested.

RateLimit.description: Structured Field List of four named policies in this order: <class>.key.second, <class>.key.minute, <class>.merchant.second, <class>.merchant.minute. r is the remaining quota after this request (refused requests do not increment); t is whole seconds until reset, rounded up to at least 1. Honor Retry-After first on a 429. Route-class quota for merchant credentials in draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11 syntax. get.description: Returns merchant payment volume buckets for the requested half-open period.

parameters.description: Inclusive period start as an RFC 3339 instant. The period is [period_start_at, period_end_at), at most 400 days, or 32 days for hour granularity.
parameters.name: period_start_at

parameters.description: Exclusive period end as an RFC 3339 instant. Omitted or future values resolve to the request time, truncated to the second.
parameters.name: period_end_at

parameters.description: ISO 4217 currency for every amount and payments_count. Defaults to the merchant's default currency. Customer and subscription counts span currencies. currencies lists the available currencies.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: Bucket size: hour, day (default), week starting Monday, or month. Buckets follow local boundaries, clipped to the period. Repeated hours have two buckets; skipped hours and days have none. Empty buckets are included.
parameters.name: granularity

parameters.description: IANA timezone for bucket boundaries. Defaults to UTC.
parameters.name: timezone

parameters.name: Flint-Version

get.description: Returns a paginated list of checkout sessions for the authenticated merchant.

parameters.description: Page size, default 20, max 100.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Cursor returned by the previous list response.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by the status each session has when read. A session past expires_at lists as expired even before its stored status is updated, unless payment work keeps it open, in which case it lists as open. A page can hold fewer sessions than page_size. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: The buyer can pay through the session.
The session collected the full amount due.
The session collected part of the amount due.
The session's deadline passed before it completed.
Another action ended the session; terminal_reason explains why.

parameters.description: Filter by Flint order ID.
parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Filter by Flint payment link ID.
parameters.name: payment_link_id

parameters.description: Filter by Flint customer ID.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Exact match on the Flint subscription plan ID.
parameters.name: subscription_plan_id

parameters.description: Exact match on the Flint invoice ID.
parameters.name: invoice_id

parameters.description: Filter by checkout surface. Sessions created before surfaces existed are hosted. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: surface

parameters.description: Filter by checkout session type. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: type

x-enum-descriptions: Pays an order that existed before the session, including a return resolution's replacement order.
Pays the order Flint created from quick_pay_item.
Signs the buyer up for subscription_plan_id. Flint created the order from the plan.
Started from the payment link in payment_link_id.

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the caller-owned external reference ID.
parameters.name: external_reference_id

parameters.description: Search across checkout session ID, external reference ID, metadata, and payment notes. Text fields match any part of the value, and %, _ and \ are ordinary characters, not wildcards. IDs match from the start and need the type prefix, such as cs_01.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by checkout_session_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.
parameters.name: sort_direction

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on expires_at.
parameters.name: expires_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on expires_at.
parameters.name: expires_before

parameters.description: Supported expansions: customer, invoice, order, payment_link. Include the requested related resources using scoped batch reads for this page. Each relationship requires its existing target read scopes. Expansion changes the representation without changing pagination tokens. Limits: at most 10 unique expand paths per request; path depth at most 2. Repeat expand, for example expand=customer&expand=invoice, or pass one comma-separated value.
parameters.name: expand

parameters.description: API version for this request. Overrides merchant and partner app defaults.
parameters.name: Flint-Version

parameters.description: Your own ID for this request, such as a log or trace ID, 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters. Flint stores it as client_request_id on the request log. The X-Request-Id response header is Flint's request ID, not this value.
parameters.name: X-Request-Id

patch.description: Updates the mutable fields of a checkout session. A merchant credential can update metadata and external_reference_id, including after the session ends. Send external_reference_id as null to clear it, or metadata as null to clear all metadata. On a session with a subscription_plan_id, either credential can send subscription_terms with the buyer's billing interval and quantity while the session is open and no payment is in progress; a change reprices the signup order and releases the delivery selection. The session's own checkout credential can also send buyer_contact and timezone while the session is open. The buyer_contact field saves the email and phone the buyer entered; send a contact field as null to clear it. post.description: Checks the code the buyer typed. A right code makes the checkout act for the customer with that email, and creates the customer, with a customer.created event, when none exists. The checkout can then save the buyer's card with save_payment_method on POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay, and list and pay with that customer's saved cards. The order's customer does not change until the payment succeeds. Only the checkout_auth_token in the response acts for that customer. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <checkout_auth_token> from then on. Every other credential for the session, including earlier checkout_auth_token values and hosted checkout links, keeps working for the checkout and acts for no customer, so it lists no saved cards and pays with none. A buyer who opens the link on another device confirms an email there to use them, and from then on only that device's new credential acts for a customer. If the response is lost after the code was accepted, the credential you sent still works. Send the same code again with it while the code is valid, which counts as another try and returns a new credential for the same customer, or request a new code. A wrong, expired, or replaced code returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_CODE_INVALID, and so does a used code once the checkout was confirmed again, any code after its 5th try, any code for an email past its limit on wrong tries, or a code whose email's customer changed its email or was deleted after the code was sent. If the checkout stops offering saved payment details before the code is confirmed, such as when the merchant turns them off, the request returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_NOT_OFFERED. A credential that already acts for a customer gets CHECKOUT_CUSTOMER_ALREADY_AUTHORIZED, and confirming never replaces a customer the merchant named. Once the customer whose email the buyer confirmed changes that email or is deleted, the checkout acts for no customer, and the buyer can confirm the customer's new email or another one. A checkout opened from a checkout reminder link acts for no customer the buyer confirmed earlier, so its buyer confirms an email again. A texted code for saved details binds the checkout the same way, but the new credential opens only the cards saved with that number: it lists and pays with no card saved by email, and reads no customer details. A texted code checks once, so after a lost answer request a new code. A code for purpose confirm_saved_payment_method keeps the session's credential, so the response omits checkout_auth_token and carries payment_method_save on the checkout session. A texted code saves the card with the number when the number already opens the customer's saved details or the customer has none yet; otherwise payment_method_save.email_confirmation_required turns true, and an emailed code finishes the save. An emailed code alone saves the card by email. After success, a retry with the same Idempotency-Key and code returns the stored answer and credential to any credential of the session. After failure, a retry checks the code again and counts as another try.

post.description: Issues a draft credit note and freezes its PDF. Provide allocation to issue and apply credit to its invoice atomically, or refund to initiate a linked refund on a paid invoice. Allocation and refund cannot be combined. Omit allocation.amount_money to apply the smaller of the credit available after issue and the invoice's outstanding balance. An explicit amount must be positive, use the invoice's currency, and fit both balances. The result includes credit_note_allocation when allocation is requested. Idempotency-Key is required and is retained for as long as the issue's effects exist, scoped to merchant, environment, credit note, and key. Reuse the key with the identical request to recover the original credit note and allocation. Recover an allocation after a lost response by listing this note's allocations with idempotency_key=issue:<issue key>. For refunds, list this note's refunds filtered by the original idempotency_key. A pending refund is accepted but has not completed. Without allocation or refund, issuance leaves the invoice balance unchanged. Issue validates the stored preview against current shared creditable pools. A fitting correction whose preview changed returns CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION with reason credit_note_creditable_value_changed: replace its existing corrections with PATCH using the current expected_version, review the recalculated amounts, and issue again. A correction exceeding the remaining pool returns CREDIT_NOTE_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_CREDITABLE. Affected historical tax allocations return ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason credit_note_tax_reconciliation_required.

Refunds use the source invoice's original payments and do not reopen its balance. Idempotency-Key is required and retained for the lifetime of the refund command, scoped to merchant, environment, credit note, and key. Reusing it with another request conflicts. Recover a lost response by listing this note's refunds with idempotency_key. A failed remainder can be requested with a new key after its outcome is definitive.

Follow pagination and inspect current and archived domains for the requested hostname; use a matching domain's custom_domain_id to retrieve its current state. Do not switch keys or wait for key retention to expire to create again. Contact support with the request_id if the outcome is still unclear.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of customers for the authenticated merchant. Without a status filter, returns active and deletion_processing customers; deleted customers appear only when the filter names deleted.

parameters.description: Filter by status. Repeat the parameter or send comma-separated values to match any of several. Omitted, the list leaves out deleted rows; name deleted to include them. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Page size, default 20, max 100.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Cursor returned by the previous list response.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Search across customer_id, name, email, phone number, and external_reference_id. Text fields match any part of the value, and %, _ and \ are ordinary characters, not wildcards. IDs match from the start and need the type prefix, such as cus_01.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the caller-owned external reference ID.
parameters.name: external_reference_id

parameters.description: Exact whole-address match after trimming surrounding whitespace, ignoring case and accents.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: Byte-sensitive whole-value match on the opaque customer segment. Whitespace, casing, Unicode, and commas are literal.
parameters.name: segment

parameters.description: Filter by merchant verification, independently of email verification.
parameters.name: is_merchant_verified

parameters.description: Exact match on a full E.164 phone number. Encode the leading plus as %2B.
parameters.name: phone

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by customer_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.
parameters.name: sort_direction

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_before

parameters.description: Supported expansions: default_payment_method, receivables. Include the requested related resources using scoped batch reads for this page. Each relationship requires its existing target read scopes. Expansion changes the representation without changing pagination tokens. Limits: at most 10 unique expand paths per request; path depth at most 2. Repeat expand, for example expand=default_payment_method&expand=receivables, or pass one comma-separated value.
parameters.name: expand

post.description: Signs the buyer in to your Flint-hosted customer account as this customer. Works for 15 minutes and one open. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same Idempotency-Key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Requires customers.sessions.write. Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this customer's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its open. Without an Idempotency-Key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with X-Request-Id before sending a new request.

delete.description: Retires the delivery method after checking current dependencies. The retired resource remains available by ID for historical records. Deleting an already archived resource returns it without changing its version or repeating effects. A method referenced by checkout.default_delivery_method_ids at merchant scope or by delivery_method_ids on an active or inactive payment link cannot be archived; the request returns 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE with the blocking references. Remove the method from checkout.default_delivery_method_ids with PATCH /v1/settings or from the link's delivery_method_ids with PATCH /v1/payment-links/{payment_link_id}. Open checkout sessions keep their pinned revision and do not block retirement.

post.description: Ends the active or provisioning demo session identified by demo_session_id for this client and provisions a fresh one. A client that lost its create response gets the current demo_session_id from the error on ACTIVE_DEMO_SESSION_EXISTS or DEMO_SESSION_SECRET_REPLAY_EXPIRED. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key and body replays the replacement before checking the current session, including its secret during the secret delivery window. After that window, the retry returns DEMO_SESSION_SECRET_REPLAY_EXPIRED. The daily cap applies only to fresh executions. Omit template to use quickstart; an explicit empty or unsupported value is invalid.

post.description: Evaluates promotion outcomes for an order without changing it. Returns the complete result inside data, without creating a resource or requiring an idempotency key. Use `promotion_id` for server-side apply flows where you already know the promotion, including code-gated promotions, which then apply without a code and count only toward the promotion's `max_uses`. Checkout credentials must use `promotion_code`. The response includes applied, skipped, and single-threshold available promotion candidates.

post.description: Upload a local image to Flint. Create a file, PUT the bytes to upload.url with upload.method and every upload.headers value, then POST /v1/files/{file_id}/complete. The URL works for 15 minutes. Purpose requires its own write scope: product and product_variant use commerce.products.write; bundle uses commerce.bundles.write; payment_link uses checkouts.payment_links.write; subscription_plan uses commerce.subscription_plans.write; merchant_logo and merchant_icon use merchants.profile.write. Logo and icon files are merchant-wide; all other purposes belong to the authenticated environment. Partner installs can upload commerce images but cannot upload merchant_logo or merchant_icon: those purposes return INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE with scope_requirement because merchants.profile.write is not grantable to installs. Idempotency is scoped to merchant, credential, environment, and route. A replay returns the original upload target without extending its expiry. After a lost response, retry with the same Idempotency-Key or create another file. Each upload URL expires 15 minutes after creation.

parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and request within 24 hours returns the original result instead of repeating it.

get.description: Returns a file's current status without upload credentials. Purpose requires its own read scope: product and product_variant use commerce.products.read; bundle uses commerce.bundles.read; payment_link uses checkouts.payment_links.read; subscription_plan uses commerce.subscription_plans.read; merchant_logo and merchant_icon use merchants.profile.read. The matching write scope also grants read access. Dashboard sessions require the purpose's manage capability. Logo and icon files are merchant-wide; other files belong to the authenticated environment. Partner installs can read commerce files but cannot read merchant_logo or merchant_icon. Expired deadlines are reflected immediately. Only ready files include url, width, and height. The response uses Cache-Control: no-store.

post.description: After PUT succeeds, complete the file to process its image. Returns the ready file; completing a ready file again returns it. Send no request body or {}. Completing before the bytes arrive returns FILE_NOT_UPLOADED and leaves the file awaiting_upload. Attach the returned file_id as images[].file_id before expires_at, 24 hours after processing. Completion requires the purpose's write scope, with the same merchant-wide branding and environment boundaries as createFile. Partner installs can upload commerce images but cannot upload merchant_logo or merchant_icon: those purposes return INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE with scope_requirement because merchants.profile.write is not grantable to installs. Idempotency is scoped to merchant, credential, environment, route, and file_id. A replay returns the original result; it does not extend upload or attachment deadlines. After a lost completion response, repeat this route with the same key and file_id.

The hold and mark_no_show actions accept reason plus an optional reason_message note. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

post.description: Record a stock change by what happened: stock received, returned, sold, stolen, lost, or moved between conditions, or an absolute count or correction. Flint computes the change against the current level. Returns the adjustment, its movement IDs, and the resulting level for every level touched. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the relevant resource or inventory movement list.

patch.description: Replace a count's complete observation set atomically. expected_version is required when replacing observations. Send every item exactly once with the count's current expected_version and each observation's required expected_physical_version. Read the level before physically counting; zero is valid for a missing level. Every assertion must match locked current stock or the whole save is refused. Preserve saved quantities and fences for unchanged lines. Recount affected items before supplying fresh fences, even when quantities are unchanged. Omitted condition quantities retain the matching level snapshot's values. occurred_at records provenance and does not reconstruct historical stock. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the relevant resource or inventory movement list.

post.description: Set action to apply or cancel an open physical count. The apply action sets inventory levels to the counted quantities and needs an observation on every line. The cancel action closes the count without changing stock. VERSION_CONFLICT on apply also covers a stale saved physical observation with no corresponding field in this request; these details omit param. Recount affected items and save the complete observations before applying again. Physical changes after observation require recounts, including at a trading location; holds and commitments alone do not invalidate observations. Stock-moving transitions return a result with inventory_count as its primary resource and inventory_levels for the levels changed. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the relevant resource or inventory movement list.

get.description: List inventory levels. Send expand=inventory_item to render each level's inventory item inline, so a stock table needs no read per row. Filter by inventory_item_status to see only the levels behind items that can be sold. Levels are strongly consistent individually, but pages may reflect different committed instants.

parameters.description: Number of resources to return.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Stable cursor returned by the previous page.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by inventory item.
parameters.name: inventory_item_id

parameters.description: Filter by Location.
parameters.name: location_id

parameters.description: Filter by the status of the inventory item the level belongs to. Only active items can be routed or reserved. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: inventory_item_status

parameters.description: True selects levels with available quantity; false selects levels with zero available quantity. Omit for all levels.
parameters.name: has_available_quantity

parameters.description: True selects levels with unavailable physical stock; false selects levels with none. Omit for all levels.
parameters.name: has_unavailable_condition

parameters.description: True selects levels with a shortage; false selects levels with none. Omit for all levels.
parameters.name: has_shortage

parameters.description: Search inventory item ID, name, SKU, or barcode. Case-insensitive substring match.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on available_quantity.
parameters.name: min_available_quantity

parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on available_quantity.
parameters.name: max_available_quantity

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_before

parameters.description: Supported expansions: inventory_item. The expansion resolves with one batched lookup per page. Expansion requires commerce.inventory.read. Limits: at most 10 unique expand paths per request; path depth at most 2. Pass expand=inventory_item.
parameters.name: expand

post.description: Set action to commit held quantity, consume committed quantity, or release held or committed quantity. Lines carry cumulative targets: resending targets already applied succeeds even after the reservation closes. supported_actions lists actions available for new changes. Stock-moving transitions return a result with inventory_reservation as its primary resource and inventory_levels for the levels changed. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the relevant resource or inventory movement list.

parameters.name: invoice_number

parameters.description: Filter by the effective collection mode. Repeat the parameter or pass comma-separated values to match multiple modes. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. parameters.description: Search across invoice_id, invoice_number, external_reference_id, recipient_email, reference, po_number, and the customer name and email on the invoice. post.description: Creates an invoice draft from exactly one source: order_id for an order-backed invoice, or quick_pay for an invoice with a new backing order. Include issue to issue it immediately, using merchant_default delivery when issue is empty. Idempotency-Key is required for every request because issuing an automatic-collection invoice can charge the buyer. Replays preserve the original invoice result and recover its current public_url only within 24 hours of the original request; later replays omit public_url. Use GET /v1/invoices/{invoice_id} for the current invoice. If Flint returns IDEMPOTENCY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED, contact Flint support with the original Idempotency-Key and request ID. Never retry with a new key.

post.description: Returns the current open invoice checkout session and aligned card attempt when they still match the invoice balance and collection run. A newly created session and attempt share the fixed expiration of the active invoice public-link generation. Unexpired sessions are reused regardless of remaining lifetime; active payment work returns a resolving conflict instead of creating competing collection. When the invoice's order has items to deliver, a new session offers the delivery methods in settings.checkout.default_delivery_method_ids, and the request fails with a validation error when those methods cannot deliver every item. return_url sets where the checkout sends the buyer after paying. A reused session takes a new return_url only until a payment starts on it, and keeps the one it has after that.

post.description: Sends short-lived confirmation codes to the current and new email addresses. If the account has no current email, only the new address must be confirmed. A rejected attempt keeps any pending email change request. Over the limit, the request returns 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with Retry-After set to the whole seconds until the oldest counted attempt leaves the window, at least 1.

Turns the optional email categories in the body on or off for the customer's current email at this merchant in the selected merchant environment, and leaves the others as they are. A customer without an email has no email preferences, and the change answers 404 with CUSTOMER_EMAIL_REQUIRED.

get.summary: List cards saved with Flint for this store

post.description: Records the buyer's consent to save an independent store copy for off-session payments, including subscriptions. Call only after the buyer agrees. Requires a live email-code buyer login and an enabled Flint wallet at a Flint-hosted store account. Supply an id from listMeFlintWalletPaymentMethods. Confirm client_setup with Stripe.js confirmSetup, then poll GET /v1/me/payment-methods/{payment_method_id} until active before changing a subscription through /v1/me/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/payment-method. Setup may request authentication. Removing the platform card or revoking store consent blocks the copy immediately. Idempotency-Key is optional and scoped to the store, customer, card handle, and key. Responses are retained for 24 hours. After a copy is revoked, retries with any key bound to that copy are refused. Get new consent and use a new key to create another copy. Retry a lost response with the same key. Concurrent requests for the same card at this store share one copy and setup. A failed off-session charge can still require the buyer to return through the existing card-update link. Accept an empty body or {}.

get.summary: Get one of the current buyer's invoices

post.description: Accepts a customer session, which limits the request to that customer's invoices, or the access token from this invoice's public link, which limits it to this invoice. The request cannot select a customer_id. Returns the current open invoice checkout session and aligned card attempt when they still match the invoice balance and collection run. A newly created session and attempt share the fixed expiration of the active invoice public-link generation. Unexpired sessions are reused regardless of remaining lifetime; active payment work returns a resolving conflict instead of creating competing collection. When the invoice's order has items to deliver, a new session offers the delivery methods in settings.checkout.default_delivery_method_ids, and the request fails with a validation error when those methods cannot deliver every item. return_url sets where the checkout sends the buyer after paying. A reused session takes a new return_url only until a payment starts on it, and keeps the one it has after that.

parameters.description: Why a closed order closed. Repeated keys and comma-separated values match any reason. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: closed_reason

parameters.description: Order status: open or closed. Repeated keys and comma-separated values are both accepted. Selecting open and closed includes both statuses. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.

parameters.description: Filter by settled collection status. Repeat the parameter or pass comma-separated values to match any of several statuses. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: payment_status

parameters.description: Filter by refund progress. Repeated keys and comma-separated values are both accepted to match any status. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: refund_status

parameters.description: Filter by aggregate order fulfillment status. Repeated keys and comma-separated values are both accepted to match any status. get.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. A typical chronological log might show created, payment_failed, payment, refund, then refund_failed; each row gives one reference to click through for the authoritative resource.

parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Filter by invoice ID.
parameters.name: invoice_id

parameters.description: Filter by payment intent status. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: Waiting for payment details. Either nothing has been attempted yet, or the last attempt was declined, failed, or blocked and last_payment_error says why. Submit payment details again to retry.
Payment details are attached, but the payment hasn't been confirmed yet. This status is brief unless the confirmation was interrupted.
A step, such as 3D Secure authentication or a redirect, must be finished before the payment can continue.
Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly.
A hold is in place on the payment method and no money has been collected. The merchant collects some or all of it, or releases it, before authorization_expires_at.
Canceled before any money was collected. Final. cancellation_reason says why when it is known. A canceled hold is in released_money.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final.
A hold reached authorization_expires_at without being collected, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. The payment_intent.expired event reports it; cancellation_reason is absent.

parameters.description: Filter by immutable payment flow. Repeat or comma-separate values. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: payment_flow

parameters.name: min_amount

parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on amount_money.amount. Requires currency.
parameters.name: max_amount

parameters.description: ISO 4217 currency for min_amount and max_amount.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: Exact match on refund_status. Repeat keys or comma-separate values to match any selected status. Combined with dispute_status, both filters must match. get.summary: Get one of the current buyer's Return resolutions

post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Create or reuse a hosted or embedded checkout session for the buyer's balance on a replacement order linked to this return resolution. Returns 200 when reusing an existing session and 201 when creating one. Omit surface to use hosted. The same surface reuses the open session; changing surface replaces an idle session and is refused while a payment is in progress. Use redirects to set where the buyer goes after paying or canceling. The return_url field is an alias for redirects.success_url on hosted checkout or payment_return_url on embedded checkout and must be an address of the merchant's customer account. A reused session takes a new success destination only until a payment starts, then keeps its existing destination.

post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Requests a Return for one of the buyer's orders. An active return policy must cover each line and leave the requested quantity eligible, or the request fails with 409 RETURN_SELF_SERVICE_NOT_ALLOWED. Check can_buyer_request with POST /v1/me/return-previews first. The buyer's reason must be active and apply to the line, and a policy that sends the request to review leaves the Return waiting for the store's decision.

get.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's subscriptions. Subscriptions without a next_billing_at never match next_billing_after or next_billing_before, and sort last with sort_by=next_billing_at in either direction. subscription_plan is always included without expand: the plan's current summary, or null when the subscription has no plan.

parameters.description: Page size, default 20, max 100.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Cursor returned by the previous list response.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by subscription status. Repeat the parameter or pass comma-separated values to match multiple statuses. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Separate subscriptions scheduled by Flint (flint) from those whose billing dates the store supplies (external). Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: billing_schedule_owner

parameters.description: When true, returns subscriptions scheduled to cancel at the end of the current period that are not yet canceled. When false, returns every other subscription.
parameters.name: cancel_at_period_end

parameters.description: Filter by the subscription's selected delivery method.
parameters.name: delivery_method_id

parameters.description: Find subscriptions needing a new delivery method, address, or rate by the current delivery_hold reason. Does not match upcoming delivery issues. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: hold_reason

parameters.description: Filter by Flint subscription plan ID.
parameters.name: subscription_plan_id

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by subscription_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.
parameters.name: sort_direction

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on next_billing_at.
parameters.name: next_billing_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on next_billing_at.
parameters.name: next_billing_before

parameters.description: Load subscriptions needing your attention. True matches subscriptions with a delivery hold, an upcoming delivery hold, or a delivery-action-required pause, plus past_due subscriptions and active or incomplete subscriptions whose billing date passed more than 24 hours ago without payment. post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Cancels a subscription and records who asked, why, and when in cancellation_details. With cancel_immediately: true it ends now. Otherwise, trialing ends at trial_end_at, active at current_period_end_at (or now when a renewal delivery hold has expired), and past_due at next_retry_at instead of that retry. Scheduled, incomplete, paused, and past_due without next_retry_at require cancel_immediately: true or return 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason period_end_unavailable. Read scheduled_cancel_at for the scheduled end time. A buyer's cancellation follows the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change.

post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Pauses a subscription immediately, optionally for at least one billing cycle. A pause with a duration resumes automatically at scheduled_resume_at. Repeating the stored pause length returns the paused subscription; a different length returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason field_locked and param pause_duration_cycles and requires resuming first. A buyer's pause follows the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change.

get.summary: List payment retries for one of the current buyer's subscriptions

post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. Starts one manual collection attempt on a past-due subscription. Send no body, or an empty object. Poll the returned retry for the outcome. While cancellation is scheduled, a new buyer retry returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason cancellation_scheduled and current_status past_due. First use POST /v1/me/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate to keep the subscription; retry_payment becomes available again if the other retry conditions allow it. Only one retry may be in progress at a time. Buyers can start a retry while fewer than 3 retries have been created for the current billing period, counting the store's retries too. subscription_card_update email-link sessions can start retries.

post.description: Creates a fresh provider session from a signed launch token after rechecking the authenticated principal, merchant environment, account controller, and component grant. An onboarding session can refresh only sandbox launch tokens created by the same user with an onboarding session. The sandbox is pinned by the launch token, which is the merchant's default sandbox for an onboarding session. Live onboarding requires a live API key or live CLI login, and refresh requires the same credential that created the launch token. A same-key, same-input retry replays the encrypted original result for 24 hours, including its original credentials and expiries. Replay may return an expired credential. Use a new key for a new launch or refresh.

parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and request within 24 hours returns the original result instead of repeating it.

get.description: Returns immutable merchant billing entries for the authenticated merchant environment, newest occurred_at first. Entries in the same second are ordered by type rank, then merchant_billing_entry_id; all three keys are descending. Type ranks are 10 for event_fee, custom_domain, and invoice; 20 for correction; 30 for credit_issued; 40 for credit_applied and credit_refunded; 50 for collection and custom_domain_collection; and 60 for collection_reversal and write_off. An entry can be recorded after entries that occurred later, such as a collection whose bank outcome arrives late. To pick up new entries, filter on created_after. Re-reading the same entry always returns the same values. To export an interval, use merchant_billing_itemized_v1. It fails with data_unavailable when billing projections or membership history are inconsistent, collection outcome or balance transaction evidence is missing, or an entry is invalid. This list does not run the report interval preflights.

parameters.description: Filter by one or more merchant billing entry types. Repeat or comma-separate values. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.

get.description: Starts a partner app install in the merchant's browser. Flint validates the request, then redirects to Flint's consent screen, where the merchant signs in, chooses a merchant, and approves or denies the requested permissions. Flint then redirects to redirect_uri with code, state, and mode, or with an OAuth error. Unknown or inactive clients and missing or unregistered redirect URIs return the Flint error envelope. Flint ignores unrecognized parameters.

post.description:
Partner apps exchange authorization codes with S256 PKCE or rotate refresh tokens for installation-scoped Bearer access tokens. A lost refresh response can be retried for 60 seconds while the replacement remains unused; a replay revokes that environment grant's token family. Authorization codes last 5 minutes and are single use. Partner access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens expire 30 days after issuance and rotate on each use. This endpoint follows OAuth token endpoint conventions: send application/x-www-form-urlencoded only. Failures return OAuth token error objects instead of the normal Flint error envelope.

The public client flint-cli supports the RFC 8628 device_code grant and rotating refresh tokens. Pending device requests return authorization_pending; early polling returns slow_down and increases the required interval by five seconds; denial returns access_denied; expired or consumed codes return expired_token. CLI access tokens last 15 minutes. CLI sessions expire after 30 days idle or 90 days total. Reusing a rotated CLI refresh token revokes its family, including when the previous response was lost. A fresh browser login is then required.

With session_mode=contexts at CLI authorization, tokens include oauth_session_id and context_id. CLI refresh requires an explicitly authorized context_id; invalid_context and context_access_denied do not consume the refresh token. Each CLI access token is limited to one context. Ordinary CLI rotation preserves other unexpired access tokens; removing consent immediately invalidates affected tokens. CLI refresh scope may request a subset of the selected grant or context scopes. Only the issued access token is narrowed; consent and other tokens are unchanged. A later refresh without scope restores the full consented scopes. Legacy CLI sessions retain their original response shape. Request rate limits return HTTP 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After and Flint-Rate-Limited-Reason. Device-code token polling returns HTTP 400 slow_down for both early polls and request rate limits.

Workload identities use grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange with subject_token, subject_token_type, and workload_identity_id. subject_token_type must be urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt or urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token. Optional scope narrows the identity scopes for this token; requested_token_type, if supplied, must be urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. Client authentication, client_id, actor_token, resource, audience, and unrecognized fields are forbidden and return invalid_request. The response includes an opaque fwat_ access token, issued_token_type, workload_identity_id, merchant_id, mode, and sandbox_id in test mode, without a refresh token. The token expires after the shorter of one hour and the remaining subject-token lifetime. Identity deactivation, archive, and scope narrowing take effect on the next API request. Exchange errors use invalid_request, invalid_grant, invalid_scope, unsupported_grant_type, temporarily_unavailable, and server_error. Limits are 300 requests per minute per IP and 600 per minute per identity after signature verification; exceeding either returns HTTP 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After and Flint-Rate-Limited-Reason. No usable external issuer keys returns HTTP 503 temporarily_unavailable.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of orders for the authenticated merchant.

parameters.description: Page size, default 20, max 100.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Cursor returned by the previous list response.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by customer ID.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on order IDs. Repeat the parameter or use comma-separated IDs to match any of up to 100 distinct IDs. Unknown IDs and orders outside your merchant or environment are absent. Other filters still apply, and results keep the list's ordering and pagination. Keep the same ID set on subsequent pages.
parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Why a closed order closed. Repeated keys and comma-separated values match any reason. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: closed_reason

parameters.description: Order status: open or closed. Repeated keys and comma-separated values are both accepted. Selecting open and closed includes both statuses. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Filter by settled collection status. Repeat the parameter or pass comma-separated values to match any of several statuses. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: payment_status

parameters.description: Filter by refund progress. Repeated keys and comma-separated values are both accepted to match any status. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: refund_status

parameters.description: Filter by aggregate order fulfillment status. Repeated keys and comma-separated values are both accepted to match any status. Accepts repeated keys, comma-separated values, or mixtures. Values are trimmed and deduplicated in first-seen order; empty or unknown entries are rejected. Values within this filter are ORed; separate filters are ANDed.
parameters.name: fulfillment_status

parameters.description: Filter by merchant-visible order number.
parameters.name: order_number

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to mutable order fields such as customer_id, notes, metadata, tax, the delivery destination, and the requested tip. A request containing only metadata, internal_note, buyer_note, or external_reference_id, with optional expected_version, can update open, closed, paid, and invoice-locked orders without changing totals. Other merchant edits keep hosted and embedded checkout sessions open unless an edit closes or completes the order, which ends the session with order_mutated. Edits can also end invoice, return-resolution, and subscription-plan sessions with order_mutated. A session already past expires_at ends with expired before the edit is applied. These annotation updates are blocked while any order payment attempt remains non-terminal, including an authorization awaiting capture, or checkout payment work is still resolving. Requests combining annotations with other fields use the financial mutation rules for the entire request. Send requested_tip: null to clear the current requested tip. A merchant can correct a paid subscription signup or renewal destination before shipment by sending delivery_destination and the current order version as expected_version. The committed delivery methods must remain eligible, and shipping and tax totals must stay unchanged. ORDER_DELIVERY_DESTINATION_REPRICE_REQUIRED returns the reason and computed shipping and tax amounts when the correction would change the paid totals.

post.description: Creates the link Flint's receipt email carries, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. It opens the order in your Flint-hosted customer account without a sign-in, and lets the buyer have the receipt sent again to the order's email. It works for 30 days or 10 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in to see the order. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same Idempotency-Key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it returns ACCESS_LINK_MERCHANT_HOSTED, and for an order without a customer, ACCESS_LINK_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an Idempotency-Key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with X-Request-Id before sending a new request.

get.description: Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. post.description: Closes an open order and stops further payment. Cancels pending discounts, releases their reservations, and recalculates totals; canceled discounts remain visible with status: "canceled" but no longer reduce the total. Unused order-owned payment intents are canceled. When collected money remains refundable, send collected_money_behavior: keep to close and keep it, or refund it first with POST /v1/refunds and order_id. Closing does not refund money; refunds remain available afterwards. Closing is blocked while payment collection is in progress. To complete a zero-balance order as paid, use POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay. closed_reason and closed_at record why and when the order closed. The request body is optional. Send expected_version to reject a mutation based on an outdated order read.

post.description: Selects a gift card by its current code and returns masked selections and an unreserved estimate. No value is held or debited. Optional expected_version must match the order version returned by the last read. An order may select at most 20 gift cards. Gift card value cannot pay for subscription orders. Retry a lost response with the same Idempotency-Key to recover the original selection result.

parameters.description: Order ID.
parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Single-use proof from the checkout's gift card challenge. Needed only after GIFT_CARD_CHALLENGE_REQUIRED. While a challenge is required, every code needs a new proof, for up to an hour after the failures that triggered it. Ignored for API keys.
parameters.name: Flint-Gift-Card-Challenge

parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and request within 24 hours returns the original result instead of repeating it.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: API version for this request. Overrides merchant and partner app defaults.
parameters.name: Flint-Version

parameters.description: Your own ID for this request, such as a log or trace ID, 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters. Flint stores it as client_request_id on the request log. The X-Request-Id response header is Flint's request ID, not this value.
parameters.name: X-Request-Id
